papers.abstract: NRG Oncology RTOG 9902 was a randomized controlled trial of the addition of adjuvant chemotherapy (paclitaxel, oral etoposide, estramustine) to long-course androgen suppression and radiation for patients with high-risk prostate cancer. The trial closed early due to excess toxicity and found no benefit to chemotherapy at a median follow-up of 9.2 years. Immediate post-radiation PSA status was dichotomized at ≤ 0.2 ng/mL. Landmark analysis redefined starting times for disease-free survival (DFS), time to distant metastasis (TDM), and overall survival (OS) at 36 weeks post-radiation, when planned chemotherapy was complete. Exclusion criteria included non-receipt of radiation or assigned chemotherapy and pre-landmark DFS events or loss to follow-up. Hazard ratios (HR), 95% confidence intervals, and PSA-by-treatment interaction estimated by Cox or competing-risks regression. Of 333 patients analyzed: 190 without and 143 with chemotherapy. Chemotherapy was associated with improved DFS for patients with PSA > 0.2 (HR 0.59, 0.38-0.91), but not for those with PSA ≤ 0.2 (HR 0.94, 0.60-1.46), interaction p = 0.13. There was no association with chemotherapy relative to post-RT PSA for either TDM or OS. This analysis suggests that men with a post-radiation PSA > 0.2 may benefit from treatment intensification with adjuvant chemotherapy. Prospective trials adapting treatment by PSA response are indicated. Trial Number: NCT00004054 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

papers.abstract: Insulin-like growth factor (IGF) signaling drives progression of glioblastoma (GBM), the most aggressive brain cancer. While sphingolipid metabolism is implicated in gliomagenesis, the mechanism by which it regulates GBM growth and therapy response is poorly understood. Through bioinformatic analyses of human gliomas, we identified sphingolipid metabolism genes with potential functional significance in glioma. Using patient-derived cells, a Drosophila glioma model, and xenograft mouse models, we investigated the functional role of Dihydroceramide desaturase 1 (DEGS1). Lipidomics profiling and RNA sequencing were performed in patient-derived cells to reveal the mechanism by which DEGS1 regulates glioma growth. Additionally, we tested the effect of a DEGS1 inhibitor on GBM cell growth and their resistance to IGF1R-targeted therapy. Our data demonstrate that the expression of sphingolipid metabolism gene DEGS1 is associated with aggressive glioma biomarkers and worse patient survival. DEGS1 is required for glioma growth in patient-derived cells, a Drosophila glioma model, and xenograft mouse models. Lipidomics profiling reveals that DEGS1 deficiency results in reduced ceramides and complex sphingolipids and accumulation of their precursors. Disrupted sphingolipid homeostasis impairs lipid raft biogenesis and lipid raft-associated IGF signaling. Targeting DEGS1 decreases GBM cell growth and their resistance to IGF1R inhibition. These findings establish that targeting DEGS1-regulated sphingolipid metabolism is a viable avenue to inhibit IGF signaling-driven GBM growth.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) develops in a nutrient-poor microenvironment and progresses from pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia (PanIN) to invasive carcinoma. Serine metabolism supports tumor growth in many cancers, spurring the development of inhibitors of phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH), the rate-limiting enzyme in serine biosynthesis. However, the limited clinical success of PHGDH inhibitors highlights the need to better understand the stage-specific role of de novo serine synthesis during PDAC progression. Here, we showed that PHGDH increases progressively from PanIN to invasive PDAC in human and mouse tissues. In genetically engineered mouse models with inducible PHGDH knockdown, PHGDH loss delayed PDAC development. Acute treatment with the PHGDH inhibitor BI-9593 suppressed de novo serine synthesis, induced cell death, and drove tumor regression. Unexpectedly, PHGDH-deficient tumors did not become more dependent on exogenous serine, and dietary serine/glycine manipulation did not affect tumor development. Instead, stable isotope tracing and metabolomic profiling showed that PHGDH loss reduced ASCT2 expression and impaired glutamine uptake and utilization, creating a metabolic liability that rendered PHGDH-deficient tumors selectively sensitive to the glutamine antagonist DRP-104. Together, these findings reveal a therapeutic vulnerability to combined metabolic targeting in PDAC.

papers.abstract: Tissue injury is a pervasive feature of human disease, yet adult mammals exhibit limited regenerative capacity. A central determinant of regenerative outcomes is the inflammatory response, which orchestrates tissue repair through mechanisms that are evolutionarily conserved from Drosophila to mammals. Following injury, inflammation drives debris clearance, promotes the release of cytokines and growth factors, and contributes to the restoration of functional cells. However, dysregulated or unresolved inflammation can impair healing, drive scar formation, and ultimately result in organ dysfunction or failure. Here, we focus on recent advances in the spatiotemporal regulation of inflammation during tissue repair that have reshaped our understanding of its underlying mechanisms. We synthesize findings on the dynamic progression of repair from inflammatory initiation to active resolution and stem cell activation, highlighting features of immune cell plasticity and heterogeneity within injury-specific microenvironments, as well as the existence of pivotal macrophage-fibroblast interactions. Furthermore, we delineate the pleiotropic and context-dependent roles of key cytokines and signaling pathways in coordinating these processes. Finally, we discuss current and emerging therapeutic strategies, emphasizing the paradigm shift from broad immunosuppression toward precise modulation of inflammatory networks to promote regeneration and prevent fibrosis. Future progress hinges on integrating multiomic spatial atlases, precision immunomodulation, and standardized therapeutic protocols to decipher and manipulate immune-regenerative crosstalk, thereby driving the development of next-generation regenerative therapies.

papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of treatment response remains challenging in cancer. To facilitate response prediction in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), we developed PRISM, an interpretable multiscale graph-learning framework for estimating treatment-specific objective response from pretreatment H&E whole-slide images. PRISM integrated multiresolution tissue representations with a cell-level tumor microenvironment (TME) hypergraph, thereby treating higher-order microenvironmental organization as a learnable component of treatment-response prediction. Samples from 7,082 patients from four Chinese centers were screened. PRISM was evaluated across treatment specific cohorts receiving targeted therapy (T), EGFR-targeted therapy (T_EGFR), immune checkpoint inhibitor-based therapy (ICI), chemoimmunotherapy (CI), and chemotherapy (C) using patient-level internal cross-validation, independent multicenter external validation, and prospective silent validation. PRISM predicted early objective responses across prespecified systemic therapies in NSCLC. In comparison to 18 established multiple-instance learning and computational pathology baseline models, PRISM remained competitive, with numerical advantages in selected tasks. Multiscale attribution and exploratory H&E-derived TME analyses provided spatial context for model predictions. Overall, PRISM offers a morphology-based framework for estimating early response to prespecified systemic therapies and warrants further prospective multicenter evaluation.

papers.abstract: Resistance to PD-1-based immunotherapy remains a major challenge in cancer treatment, especially in immunologically "cold" tumors characterized by T-cell exclusion and impaired T-cell effector function. Mechanical processes impact T-cell activity, and mechanical perturbations may represent a distinct mode of immune suppression. Here, we identified CD209, a myeloid-expressed C-type lectin receptor, as a mechanosuppressive regulator of antitumor T-cell immunity. CD209 was selectively enriched in tumor-infiltrating M2-like macrophages and monocytes, and elevated CD209 expression was associated with poor clinical response to PD-1 blockade and immune dysfunction and exclusion across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, CD209 directly engaged ICAM-2 on T cells and activated ROCK1-ERM signaling. This interaction increased T-cell cortical stiffness, destabilized T cell-antigen presenting cell interactions, and attenuated T-cell receptor signaling. Blocking the CD209-ICAM-2-ERM pathway restored T-cell activation and promoted CD8+ T-cell infiltration and effector function in both in vivo mouse models and ex vivo human tumor systems. Importantly, CD209 blockade enhanced the response to PD-1 inhibition and overcame resistance to PD-1-based immunotherapy in refractory and immunologically "cold" tumor models. Together, these findings define a myeloid-derived mechanical immune checkpoint and reveal T-cell mechanosuppression as a targetable mechanism of tumor immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance.

papers.abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) measures cortical hemodynamics, yet its ability to characterize anesthesia-related functional changes remains unclear. This exploratory secondary analysis used prospectively collected data from 120 female patients undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under propofol or sevoflurane anesthesia (60 per group). Twenty-channel prefrontal fNIRS recordings covered wakefulness, induction, and maintenance. Deoxygenated hemoglobin-derived amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF), functional connectivity (FC), network topology, and within- and cross-state FC similarity were assessed. Support vector machine, logistic regression, and random forest classifiers assessed discrimination between states. During induction, ALFF increased by 89.8% to 202.2% with propofol and 75.2% to 242.0% with sevoflurane across five prefrontal regions (all P < 0.001). During maintenance, mean ALFF was below awake levels, with significant reductions of 20.0% to 40.1% in three regions under sevoflurane (all P ≤ 0.019). Induction-related FC changes were limited and regionally heterogeneous. Regional FC, modularity, and global efficiency showed no significant maintenance-versus-awake differences in either group. Within-state between-subject FC similarity was significantly higher during maintenance than during wakefulness only with sevoflurane (mean difference [MD], 0.110; 95% CI, 0.054 to 0.169; P < 0.001). Cross-state between-subject FC similarity was higher for awake-maintenance than awake-induction comparisons with propofol (MD, 0.072; 95% CI, 0.055 to 0.090) and sevoflurane (MD, 0.144; 95% CI, 0.126 to 0.161; both P < 0.001). Support vector machine classification of induction versus wakefulness yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.83 (95% CI, 0.75 to 0.90) for propofol and 0.85 (95% CI, 0.78 to 0.91) for sevoflurane; maintenance-versus-awake AUCs were 0.67 (95% CI, 0.58 to 0.75) and 0.76 (95% CI, 0.68 to 0.85). Prefrontal fNIRS detected widespread induction-related hemodynamic changes, but the present connectivity measures provided limited discrimination between maintenance of anesthesia and wakefulness.

papers.abstract: Brain neoplasms cause substantial morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries, yet structural and geographic factors in access and outcomes are poorly quantified. Using discharge data from Mexico's Ministry of Health hospitals, we examined access to brain tumor surgery and the relationship between facility level and mortality. We retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing brain tumor surgery in Ministry of Health hospitals using the national discharge registry (2010-2022). Multivariable logistic regression with hospital-clustered standard errors assessed associations of facility level and travel time with in-hospital mortality, adjusting for clinical and socioeconomic covariates. We also examined timely access among patients and in the population. Among 10,532 patients, 74.4% reached care within 2 h, and 68.0% of the population lived within 2 h of a Ministry of Health level 3 neurosurgical center, below the 80% Lancet Commission benchmark. Indigenous community, pediatric age, and male sex were associated with lower odds of timely access. Surgery at a level 2 versus level 3 hospital was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (OR 1.25; 95% CI 1.01-1.56; sensitivity range 1.22-1.40), and travel time, less consistently, with a modest increase (OR 1.04 per hour beyond 2 h; 95% CI 1.00-1.07). Malignancy, older age, and pediatric age were associated with higher mortality. Within Mexico's Ministry of Health hospitals, brain tumor surgery is geographically concentrated, and surgery at level 2 hospitals was associated with higher in-hospital mortality. These findings warrant evaluation of level 2 neurosurgical capacity and referral pathways to tertiary centers.

papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, largely due to tumor heterogeneity, late diagnosis, and high recurrence rates even after curative treatment. Although HCC is potentially curable when detected at an early stage, suboptimal surveillance, particularly in patients with underlying cirrhosis or metabolic risk factors, limits the proportion of patients eligible for curative therapies. Current surveillance strategies for at-risk populations have intrinsic limitations, and the performance of imaging and serum biomarkers remains suboptimal. Moreover, the lack of reliable prognostic biomarkers for detecting early recurrence hampers post-treatment surveillance and impacts clinical outcomes. In this context, circulating biomarkers have emerged as promising tools for improving both early detection and prognostic stratification. Liquid biopsy has the potential to enable early, non-invasive diagnosis of HCC and allows longitudinal assessment of tumor progression through serial sampling. In early-stage HCC, blood candidates may complement or outperform conventional approaches by enabling earlier diagnosis and more accurate risk stratification. In this review, we summarize recent advances and current challenges in the clinical translation of circulating biomarkers. We focus on key liquid biopsy components, including circulating cell-free DNA, particularly circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, non-coding RNAs, extracellular vesicles, proteins and metabolites, such as bile acids and lipids, highlighting their diagnostic and prognostic potential and their possible integration into personalized management strategies for patients with early-stage HCC.

papers.abstract: Cancer incidence continues to increase globally, with many patients diagnosed during working age. Employment disruption after cancer diagnosis is an important survivorship and socioeconomic issue, yet long-term evidence across cancer types and patient subgroups remains limited. This study evaluated unemployment risk and workforce attrition among workers after cancer diagnosis. We conducted a nationwide cohort study of workers aged 18 to 60 years newly diagnosed with cancer between 2011 and 2020, with follow-up of up to 12 years. Noncancer workers were selected using 1:1 hybrid matching based on demographic, clinical, and insurance characteristics. The primary outcome was unemployment, defined as transition from employee status to dependent or local administrative enrollment without dependent eligibility for at least 12 months. Workforce attrition, defined as unemployment or death, was evaluated as a secondary outcome. Competing risk and Cox regression models were applied. After matching, 119,200 pairs of cancer and noncancer workers were included. The cumulative incidence of unemployment among cancer workers was 7.9% at 1 year and 32.5% at 12 years, compared with 5.3% and 22.9% among noncancer workers. Cancer diagnosis was associated with higher unemployment risk (subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.48 to 1.54). Risks were greatest among women, individuals aged 40 to 49 years, and those with advanced-stage disease. Cancer was also associated with an approximately threefold higher risk of workforce attrition. Cancer diagnosis was associated with substantial long-term employment disruption. These findings highlight the need for survivorship-oriented workforce support and employment protection strategies.

papers.abstract: Tailgut cysts are rare congenital retrorectal lesions. Because the risk of malignancy remains uncertain, resection has historically been recommended even for asymptomatic patients. We examined whether clinical and imaging features can identify patients suitable for active surveillance. Patients diagnosed with a tailgut cyst at a tertiary cancer center between 1996 and 2021 were identified from radiology and pathology databases. Demographic, clinical, imaging, operative, pathologic, and oncologic data were reviewed. Management was individualized after multidisciplinary review. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Fifty-four patients were included; 47 (87%) had benign disease and 7 (13%) had malignant disease. Malignancy was present at diagnosis in all cases and occurred exclusively in symptomatic patients. Malignancy was associated with older age (median 57 vs. 45 years, p = 0.036) and rectal pain at presentation (86% vs. 30%, p = 0.008). On imaging, malignant cysts were significantly larger and more likely to demonstrate solid components, calcifications, and adjacent structure involvement. Twenty patients with benign-appearing cysts were enrolled in active surveillance. In this cohort, no malignant events were observed during follow-up, with a 5-year cancer-free survival of 100%. Five-year overall survival was 28.6% for malignant versus 91.9% for benign cysts (p < 0.0001). Malignant tailgut cysts appear to represent a clinically and radiographically distinct subset present at diagnosis. Asymptomatic patients with benign-appearing cysts demonstrated excellent long-term outcomes under active surveillance. These findings suggest that a risk-adapted management strategy incorporating symptoms and imaging features may help guide selection between surgery and surveillance.

papers.abstract: While nanomedicines hold great promise for solid tumour therapy, their penetration and access to tumour cells is limited by large glycosylated proteins called mucins that are enriched in the tumour microenvironment. Here we show that mucins induce the disassembly of self-assembled mPEG-polyester micellar nanoparticles into smaller unimers. Leveraging this finding, we designed a mucin-responsive, paclitaxel-conjugated nanomedicine (mrPNM) whose unimers are capable of escaping the mucin-binding barrier. Following intravenous injection, this designer mucin-responsive nanomedicine exhibited markedly deeper penetration than the mucin-nonresponsive nanomedicine and albumin, resulting in 3.9- and 1.5-fold increases in tumour cell delivery, respectively, in a pancreatic mouse tumour model. The mrPNMs also achieved superior tumour growth inhibition compared to both the mucin-nonresponsive nanomedicine and Abraxane, the FDA-approved nanoparticle albumin-bound paclitaxel, in three solid tumour models. The mucin-responsive nanomedicine platform could provide a general strategy for improving the treatment of solid tumours.

papers.abstract: Aneuploidy and chromosomal instability are common characteristics of cancer but remain underexploited therapeutically. Chromosomally unstable cells are often selectively vulnerable to inhibition of the kinesin KIF18A, and this dependence is related to altered mitotic control. Here, we identify the spindle and kinetochore-associated (SKA) complex as a mitotic regulator that establishes a similar dependency. SKA complex loss is tolerated in cells with a defective mitotic checkpoint, but when mitosis is prolonged, it leads to mitotic errors and loss of viability. Genetic analysis reveals that the SKA complex and KIF18A are epistatic, although they function through mechanistically distinct mitotic pathways. SKA complex depletion selectively impacts chromosomally unstable cancer cells and mirrors the effects of KIF18A inhibition. We thus identify a cellular vulnerability associated with prolonged mitosis in chromosomally unstable cancers.

papers.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is characterized by pronounced molecular heterogeneity and remains incurable in a substantial fraction of patients who relapse or develop refractory disease following standard chemoimmunotherapy. PIM kinases are constitutively active oncogenic serine/threonine kinases implicated in lymphoma pathogenesis, transcriptional control and cell viability. However, the detailed molecular mechanisms by which PIMs regulate transcriptional programs, RNA metabolism, and genome stability remain largely unknown. Here, we demonstrate that PIM kinases maintain interphase phosphorylation of histone H3 at serine 10 (H3S10ph). Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of PIM kinase family leads to a global reduction of H3S10ph and other active histone marks, impaired RNA polymerase II elongation, and widespread transcriptional repression. Integrated epigenomic and transcriptomic analyses reveal that PIM family inhibition preferentially affects gene networks involved in RNA metabolism, including RNA processing, splicing, and RNA methylation pathways. PIM1 proximity proteome analysis identified multiple splicing-related proteins, and PIM1 co-association with SF3B1, XAB2, and EDC3 was confirmed using co-immunoprecipitation. Functionally, PIM kinase inhibition induces extensive alternative mRNA splicing abnormalities, promotes the accumulation of RNA-DNA hybrids (R-loops), and triggers DNA damage-associated checkpoint responses. Consistent with these findings, in preliminary in vitro drug combination studies, PIM inhibition synergizes with DNA-damaging chemotherapy and targeted inhibitors of the DNA damage response. Collectively, our results implicate PIM kinases in the regulation of transcription, RNA metabolism, and genome stability in DLBCL and provide a preclinical rationale for further investigation of combinations of PIM inhibitors with DNA-damaging agents or DNA damage response inhibitors.

papers.abstract: Myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS) are clonal myeloid neoplasms characterized by ineffective hematopoiesis, cytopenias, and a variable risk of transformation to Acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Although genetic lesions are central to MDS pathogenesis, progression to AML cannot be explained by mutation accumulation alone. This review synthesizes evidence that MDS-to-AML transformation is a dynamic ecological process driven by reciprocal interactions between mutant hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell clones and the bone marrow immune microenvironment. In normal marrow, hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, T cells, NK(natural killer) cells, myeloid cells, mesenchymal stromal cells, endothelial cells, and the extracellular matrix maintain hematopoietic homeostasis and immune surveillance. In MDS, chronic inflammation coexists with impaired immune effector function, including T-cell exhaustion, reduced NK-cell cytotoxicity, expansion of myeloid-derived suppressor cells and immunosuppressive regulatory T-cell subsets, monocyte-macrophage reprogramming, mesenchymal stromal cell dysfunction, extracellular matrix remodeling, and metabolic adaptation. Together, these alterations establish a proinflammatory but immunosuppressive niche that weakens clearance of abnormal clones while providing stromal and metabolic support for clonal expansion and treatment resistance. Mutant clones further remodel the niche through epigenetic silencing, altered chemokine and cytokine signaling, and inflammatory-metabolic reprogramming, generating positive-feedback circuits that link inflammation, DNA damage, immune escape, increasing clonal burden, and therapy resistance. This review discusses how integrating clonal genetics with immune, stromal, and metabolic features may refine risk stratification and inform microenvironment-directed combination therapies. Longitudinal single-cell and spatial profiling will be essential for identifying reversible immune dysfunction and developing individualized strategies to delay or prevent AML transformation.

papers.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) lacks effective disease-modifying therapy. This study evaluated the protective effects of irbesartan (Ir), explored fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 (FGFR1) as a candidate molecular mediator, and assessed whether cRGD modification could enhance nanoparticle uptake and local treatment effects. Rat IDD models and IL-1β-induced degenerative nucleus pulposus cells were used to assess free Ir and Ir-loaded cRGD-modified PLGA nanoparticles (cRGD-NPs@Ir). Bioinformatics screening, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and molecular docking were used to nominate FGFR1 as a candidate Ir-associated protein, and FGFR1 knockdown was used to test whether FGFR1 status modified the treatment response. Imaging, histology, immunohistochemistry, Western blotting, RT-qPCR, nanoparticle characterization, Coumarin-6 uptake assays, and tandem LC3 reporter analysis were used to evaluate treatment-associated changes. Ir attenuated structural and molecular features of IDD, reduced MAPK/NF-κB signaling, altered autophagy-associated markers, and preserved extracellular matrix homeostasis. FGFR1 expression was lower in degenerative disc tissue, and FGFR1 knockdown attenuated several protective changes associated with Ir or cRGD-NPs@Ir. cRGD-NPs@Ir produced greater carrier-associated Coumarin-6 uptake than NPs@Ir and larger treatment-associated changes than free Ir for several directly compared endpoints. These findings support an FGFR1-related component of the response but do not establish direct Ir-FGFR1 binding, receptor-specific cRGD targeting, or exclusive FGFR1 dependence. FGFR1 may contribute as a candidate molecular mediator to Ir-associated changes in autophagy and inflammatory signaling in IDD. cRGD-NPs@Ir provides an uptake-enhancing local nanodelivery strategy, although receptor specificity and direct Ir-FGFR1 binding require further validation.

papers.abstract: A comprehensive understanding of the Ras self-inactivation mechanism at atomic resolution-specifically, intrinsic GTP hydrolysis converting the GTP-bound active form to the GDP-bound inactive form-is essential for designing therapies against Ras-driven cancers. Conventional models describe a biphasic GTP-bound state: Ras interconverts between inactive state 1 and active, catalytically competent state 2. However, the structural pathway leading to Ras/GDP via these states remains unclear. Here, we use time-resolved serial femtosecond and synchrotron crystallography to capture GTP hydrolysis in Ras crystals loaded with photoactivatable caged GTP, across timescales from milliseconds to hours. Photolysis yielded Ras in state 1-a conformation lacking a stabilized nucleophilic water characteristic of state 2. Remarkably, this state persists for hours and converts directly to Ras/GDP without passing through state 2. These findings challenge the prevailing view that state 2 is essential and suggest that state 1 can directly support catalysis, offering an alternative conceptual basis for targeting clinically relevant Ras mutants that preferentially adopt this conformation.

papers.abstract: Current understanding of the host tissue response to solid tumours is largely based on investigations of tumour types in isolation1. Given the breadth and diversity of human tumour pathology and contributions of tumour microenvironment (TME) cells to disease progression, pan-cancer analysis is needed to bridge major themes of stromal and immune cell evolution. To date, however, efforts to compare the TME response across cancers have been limited in scope2,3. Here we conduct a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis by algorithmically screening thousands of publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets for stromal and immune signatures across species and tissue types. We demonstrate conserved hallmarks of host cell transcriptional programming in response to malignancy across 42 cancer types in more than 2,000 human and mouse tumour samples. These findings are codified as an interactive web atlas ( tmeatlas.stanford.edu ) and software package (scTME) that will serve as practical resources for the systematic interrogation of the TME in tumours.

papers.abstract: Ferroptosis, a form of cell death induced by overwhelming membrane lipid peroxidation, is a vulnerability of many cancers, including cancers resistant to current molecular and immune-based therapies1-7. Triggering of ferroptosis therefore provides an opportunity to achieve elimination of difficult-to-treat cancers1-4,8,9. Studies in mouse cancer models have demonstrated that anticancer immunity, mediated by dendritic cells (DCs) and CD8+ T cells, is essential for effective tumour eradication by ferroptosis-inducing strategies10-13. However, ferroptotic cells limit this response8-10,14, resulting in immune escape and tumour growth through mechanisms that remain unclear. Here we demonstrate that ferroptotic cancer cells activate a molecular program resulting in aberrant production of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), which limits the stimulation of anticancer CD8+ T cell responses by type 1 conventional DCs (cDC1s), thereby promoting immune escape. In ferroptotic cancer cells, lipid peroxidation-mediated membrane permeabilization enables Ca2+ influx, which activates p38 MAPK signalling and thereby drives PGE2 production. This signalling axis is uncoupled from cancer cell death and can be targeted to selectively interfere with immune-inhibitory PGE2 production while preserving ferroptotic cancer cell elimination. In the context of cancer cell ferroptosis, ablation of PGE2 production or disrupting PGE2 signalling restores cDC1-mediated anticancer CD8+ T cell responses and leads to effective tumour elimination. Our findings identify a key mechanism that limits antitumour immunity and prevents tumour elimination upon ferroptosis induction in cancer cells, which could be exploited for cancer therapy.

papers.abstract: Lymph node metastasis (LNM) is central to breast cancer staging and treatment decisions. Clinical observations indicate that luminal or hormone receptor-positive breast cancer may show a distinct clinical pattern of regional lymph node involvement, but the stromal and intracellular mechanisms remain unclear. We integrated Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) data, a multicenter institutional cohort, public single-cell RNA sequencing data, spatial transcriptomics, and multiplex immunofluorescence. Fibroblast states and candidate cell-cell communication pathways were examined using CytoTRACE, pseudotime, and ligand-receptor analyses. Functional and mechanistic validation included co-culture and Transwell assays, a mouse footpad-popliteal lymph node metastasis model, immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, co-immunoprecipitation, protein stability assays, and ubiquitination assays. Group comparisons used parametric or nonparametric tests, as appropriate. The SEER and multicenter cohorts showed a higher proportion of lymph node involvement in HR-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer than in the HER2-positive and triple-negative groups. Single-cell analysis identified a TINAGL1 + CAF population enriched in lymph node metastases, and spatial analysis demonstrated its proximity to epithelial tumor cells. Ligand-receptor analysis and tissue imaging supported MDK-SDC4 as a candidate stromal-tumor communication axis. Fibroblast-derived MDK promoted tumor-cell migration and invasion, and these responses were attenuated by SDC4 knockdown. Mechanistically, SDC4 associated with RELB and regulated its ubiquitination and proteasomal stability. USP9X associated with SDC4 and RELB, and USP9X perturbation altered RELB ubiquitination and protein stability. In vivo, SDC4 knockdown and overexpression produced opposite changes in imaging signals and popliteal lymph node volume, while RELB or USP9X knockdown attenuated the phenotype associated with SDC4 overexpression. Histological and immunohistochemical examination provided additional tissue-level characterization of the lymph node lesions. Fibroblast-derived MDK promotes breast cancer cell migration and invasion through tumor-cell SDC4. In vitro and in vivo findings support an SDC4-USP9X-RELB regulatory axis involving RELB ubiquitination and stability, providing mechanistic insight into stromal-tumor communication in regional lymph node metastasis.

papers.abstract: Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed breast cancer treatment, predicting durable clinical benefit remains challenging. Current biomarkers, primarily derived from tumor tissue or peripheral blood, do not directly capture the adaptive immune response at its site of initiation. Tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) are not passive conduits for metastasis but dynamic immunological hubs where anti-tumor T cell priming and immune evasion converge. In this review, we critically examine the nascent intersection of TDLN immunobiology, high-resolution multi-omics, and artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate TDLN-derived features as candidate next-generation biomarkers for immunotherapy. We synthesize the complex cellular and molecular architecture of the breast cancer TDLN, including T cell exhaustion, B cell-mediated immunity, and stromal crosstalk, before evaluating the state-of-the-art single-cell and spatial technologies capable of decoding this microenvironment. We assess the application of AI and foundation models in this domain, identifying a major methodological gap: while AI frameworks are increasingly mature for primary tumors, their application to TDLNs remains unvalidated and limited by a severe scarcity of annotated multi-omics datasets. Furthermore, we address pivotal translational considerations, including the immunological implications of axillary surgery in the ICI era. We emphasize that no TDLN-derived biomarker has yet undergone prospective validation as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy in breast cancer, and that retrospective analyses of trial specimens must account for the timing of tissue acquisition relative to systemic therapy. Finally, we chart immediate research priorities, including establishing TDLN reference atlases and developing clinically feasible specimen collection pathways for biomarker validation. This review provides a conceptual framework and translational roadmap to assess whether TDLN-derived features can complement existing tumor-centric metrics in guiding immunotherapy decisions.

papers.abstract: Research on tumor metabolic reprogramming has long centered on glucose, lipids and free amino acids. By contrast, di/tripeptides, which lie at the interface between protein breakdown products and functional metabolic signals, have only recently begun to be recognized as a distinct molecular tier in cancer biology. Compared with longer peptides, di/tripeptides display greater metabolic mobility and a clearer dependence on dedicated transport systems. Here we systematically review the sources, transport, metabolic use, biological functions and clinical translational potential of di/tripeptides in cancer. Current evidence indicates that di/tripeptides arise from endogenous protein degradation, dietary digestion and microbial metabolism. Under nutrient limitation, tumor cells can recover amino acids through carnosine dipeptidase 2 (CNDP2)-mediated extracellular cleavage of dipeptides or uptake of intact di/tripeptides followed by intracellular hydrolysis. Beyond their role as nutrient substrates, selected di/tripeptides directly influence tumor cell proliferation, invasion, metastasis and drug resistance, and shape the tumor microenvironment by modulating acid base balance, redox homeostasis, angiogenesis and immune cell function. At the clinical translational level, di/tripeptides have emerged as candidate metabolomic and peptidomic biomarkers, transporter targeted imaging probes, functionally modified therapeutic agents and engineered delivery modules. Di/tripeptides should be viewed as molecular nodes that connect tumor nutrient adaptation, signaling control, microenvironmental remodeling and clinical translation, with significance extending beyond their role as transient intermediates in protein metabolism.

papers.abstract: Extramedullary disease (EMD) predicts poor outcomes after B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM). KQ-2003 is a bicistronic BCMA/CD19 CAR T-cell product incorporating 4-1BB and CD28-YMFM costimulatory domains. We assessed its activity and intralesional biology, focusing on EMD. Twenty-four patients received KQ-2003 (21 trial participants; three compassionate-use patients). Hematologic and EMD responses were assessed using International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) and Italian Myeloma criteria for PET Use, respectively. Bone marrow minimal residual disease (MRD) was assessed by next-generation flow cytometry (10- 5 sensitivity). Progression-free survival (PFS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox methods. Longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing profiled one patient's infusion product, serial blood, and spatially distinct EMD biopsies. Patients had received a median of five prior lines; 18 (75.0%) were triple-class refractory, six (25.0%) penta-refractory, 23 (95.8%) had high-risk cytogenetics, and 15 (62.5%) had EMD. All 20 patients with measurable hematologic disease achieved hematologic responses (18 [90.0%] complete/stringent complete); IMWG-defined overall response rate was 95.0%. Fourteen (93.3%) of 15 EMD patients achieved metabolic responses (13 [86.7%] complete). Among 19 baseline MRD-positive patients, 12 (63.2%) became MRD-negative by month 6; 10 and six also had documented negativity at months 12 and 24, respectively. At 29.2 months' median follow-up, median PFS was 24.0 months (95% CI, 15.0-not reached); no significant difference was detected by baseline EMD status (HR, 0.92; P = 0.89). Among the 21 trial participants, grade ≥ 3 cytokine release syndrome and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome occurred in one (4.8%) and two (9.5%), respectively; two treatment-related fatal pneumonias occurred. Single-patient longitudinal profiling revealed proliferating lesion-infiltrating CAR T cells with increased CCL3/CCL4 expression and tumor-cell apoptotic and necroptotic transcriptional programs. Trajectory analysis suggested transcriptional links between tissue effectors and circulating CCL5-positive memory-like CAR T cells. CellChat predicted BCMA-related tumor-microenvironment interactions and immune-cell interactions involving circulating CAR T cells. KQ-2003 produced deep, durable hematologic and metabolic responses in heavily pretreated, high-risk RRMM, including EMD. Intralesional profiling identified CAR T-cell proliferation, tumor-cell death-associated programs, and candidate microenvironmental interactions. These findings warrant further evaluation of this dual-targeting strategy in EMD. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04714827; registered 19 January 2021.

papers.abstract: Heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPGs) and their degrading enzyme heparanase (Hpse) play pivotal roles in tumor invasion and metastasis. Previous studies have reported associations between Hpse expression in tumor cells and patient prognosis. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are a cornerstone of solid tumor therapy, the role of Hpse in antitumor immunity remains unclear. Here, we examined Hpse localization and its impact on the immune microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma. To investigate the relationships among the Hpse expression, tumor prognosis, and tumor-infiltration of immune cells, an immunohistochemical analysis of Hpse1, Hpse2, regulatory T cells (Tregs), macrophages, and CD8+ T cells was performed in resected tumor tissue from lung adenocarcinoma patients. The effects of the Hpse inhibitor PG545 on the invasive capabilities of lymphocytes were investigated. In lung adenocarcinoma tissues, Hpse1 and Hpse2 were expressed in both epithelial tumor cells and immune cells. A high Hpse1 expression and low Hpse2 expression are poor postoperative prognostic factors in both epithelial cells and tumor-infiltrating hematopoietic cells. Single-cell RNA sequencing of human tumor-infiltrating immune cells revealed that Tregs and some subclusters of macrophages specifically express Hpse1. Lung adenocarcinoma tissue with high Hpse-expressing immune cells demonstrated an increase in tumor-infiltrating Tregs. PG545 suppressed the invasion of Tregs toward the HSPG-containing ECM. Furthermore, PG545 suppressed tumor progression and infiltration of Tregs in a mouse model. In addition, PG545 reinforced antitumor effects of PD-L1 blockade. Hpse expression in Tregs has a significant impact on lung cancer progression and is a promising therapeutic target for novel combination immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Ultrasound-guided radial artery cannulation is common in pediatrics but technically challenging. While the ulnar artery is a potential alternative, its sonoanatomy relative to the radial artery is not well defined. This study aimed to compare the sonoanatomic characteristics of the radial and ulnar arteries in children, evaluating how age, weight, and wrist position (0°, 30°, and 45°) influence arterial dimensions and depth to identify the most favorable profile for cannulation. Ultrasound evaluation of the radial and ulnar arteries was performed at 0°, 30°, and 45° wrist extension in 180 anesthetized children aged 0-120 months using custom-made wooden blocks. Arterial dimensions and skin-to-artery distance were evaluated overall and across age (≤ 24 vs. > 24 months) and weight (≤ 12 vs. > 12 kg) subgroups to identify optimal access conditions. Wrist extension angle did not significantly affect anteroposterior diameter (1.4 ± 0.3 mm, p = 0.078), but significantly influenced transverse arterial diameter (1.5-1.6 mm, p = 0.003) and skin-to-artery distance (2.4-2.8 mm at 30°, p < 0.001). The radial artery was widest at 0° (1.6 ± 1.0 mm), while the ulnar artery peaked at 30° (1.6 ± 0.4 mm). Skin-to-artery distance was minimized at 30° for both vessels. In children ≤ 12 kg, radial transverse diameter decreased paradoxically from 0° to 45° (1.6 ± 0.4 to 1.4 ± 0.3 mm, p = 0.013), while the ulnar artery was widest at 30° (1.5 ± 0.3 mm, p = 0.007). In infants ≤ 24 months, wrist angle did not significantly influence radial artery depth (p = 0.631, mean overall depth between 2.5-2.6 mm). A 30° wrist extension angle provides the most favorable sonoanatomic profile for both arteries. Although a larger vessel caliber may potentially facilitate cannulation, its clinical benefit remains uncertain as cannulation outcomes were not assessed. These findings support individualized ultrasound-guided assessment rather than a fixed positioning strategy.

papers.abstract: Rapid advances in antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and an expanding clinical evidence base are reshaping treatment options for hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) metastatic breast cancer (mBC). Randomized trials have demonstrated progression-free survival benefits over chemotherapy for individual ADCs in defined populations, including settings before and after metastatic chemotherapy. As additional ADCs become available and indications expand, attention is increasingly focused on whether individual agents can improve outcomes over endocrine-based regimens in selected endocrine-eligible patients and on which therapies beyond conventional chemotherapy may retain activity after ADC progression. Addressing these questions requires integration of clinical evidence with a mechanistic understanding of ADC activity and resistance. In this review, we summarize selected mechanisms of ADC action and critically examine the evolving clinical roles of individual agents across settings defined by prior therapy. We also discuss treatment strategies after ADC exposure and resistance mechanisms relevant to target and payload selection. Finally, we review exploratory studies of candidate biomarkers associated with clinical outcomes, ADC-based combinations, and next-generation designs, highlighting their biological rationale, emerging evidence, and priorities for further evaluation.

papers.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) support local adaptive immunity and are associated with favorable antitumor responses across multiple cancers. However, how anticancer treatment reshapes TLS maturation, particularly in lung cancer brain metastasis (LCBM), remains poorly understood. We integrated clinicopathological profiling of LCBM cohorts with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial profiling, immune-repertoire analysis, histological validation, and murine intracranial tumor models. Associations between prior treatment and TLS maturation were evaluated using multivariable analyses. Mechanistic studies examined chemotherapy-associated IL-33 release, mast-cell activation, and the effects of PGD2 on antigen-specific T-cell cytotoxicity and B-cell differentiation. Pharmacological inhibition of H-PGDS and mast-cell stabilization were further evaluated in vivo. Mature TLSs were associated with favorable survival in patients with LCBM, whereas preoperative chemotherapy was independently associated with impaired TLS maturation after adjustment for measured clinical and treatment covariates. Consistent with this observation, chemotherapy-treated tumors exhibited increased IL-33 levels, mast-cell accumulation, and enhanced mast-cell degranulation, with spatial analyses placing activated mast cells within TLS-associated immune niches. Mechanistically, IL-33 activated ST2-expressing mast cells, induced NF-κB-associated transcriptional programs. Functionally, mast cell-derived PGD2 suppressed antigen-specific CD8⁺ T-cell cytotoxicity and impaired plasma-cell differentiation, providing a potential link between chemotherapy and weakened local adaptive immunity. In vivo, pharmacological inhibition of H-PGDS enhanced chemotherapy efficacy, while mast-cell stabilization with cromolyn sodium reduced chemotherapy-associated degranulation, increased local adaptive immune-cell infiltration, improved intracranial tumor control, and prolonged survival when combined with chemotherapy. Our findings support a model in which chemotherapy-associated tissue stress activates an IL-33-responsive mast-cell program and restrains TLS-associated adaptive immunity in LCBM. Although this pathway is unlikely to operate as an exclusively linear or mast-cell-specific mechanism, targeting mast-cell-associated inflammatory signaling may provide a strategy to preserve antitumor immunity and improve the therapeutic efficacy of chemotherapy in brain metastasis.

papers.abstract: Salvage stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) for selected patients with recurrent IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (rGB) offers survival benefit, but optimal dosing remains undefined. We evaluated safety, efficacy, and dose-response relationships of single fraction SRS for rGB. We conducted a retrospective multicenter study of 271 consecutive patients with rGB treated with single-fraction SRS at first recurrence (2007-2025). Primary outcome was post-recurrence survival (PRS); secondary outcomes included overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). Multivariable Cox regression, propensity score matching (PSM), and recursive partitioning analysis (RPA) were used to identify prognostic factors. Median age was 61 years; 63% male. Median recurrent tumor volume was 3.0 cm³ (IQR, 0.8-8.7). Median single fraction SRS dose was 16 Gy (IQR, 14-19). Radiation necrosis and neurological deficits occurred in 5.5% and 8.2%, respectively. Median PRS, OS, and PFS were 12.3, 24.2, and 10.4-months. Higher SRS dose independently predicted longer PRS (HR 0.81/Gy; 95% CI 0.73-0.90, p 19 Gy improved PRS (18.6 vs 11.3-months; p=0.002) without increased toxicity in PSM cohorts. MGMT methylation and unifocal recurrence were favorable prognostic factors. In the RPA, tumor volume was the primary prognostic factor; dose intensification benefited mainly patients with smaller tumors, while preserved performance status reduced risk in larger tumors. Kaplan-Meier curves confirmed clinically meaningful PRS stratification (p<0.001). SRS is safe and effective for select patients with first-recurrence GB. Higher prescription doses were associated with improved post-recurrence survival without added toxicity within the dose range and volumes studied with a substantial number of patients receiving bevacizumab within 30 days of SRS. Dose-intensified SRS may be considered in carefully selected patients with limited-volume recurrence and preserved performance status.

papers.abstract: To report a single arm multi-site phase II study evaluating a reduced contralateral neck elective nodal clinical target volume (enCTV) in p16+ oropharyngeal cancer (p16+OPC). Newly diagnosed p16+OPC without contralateral nodal involvement but with clinical or pathological features warranting contralateral elective nodal treatment were eligible. Treatment included proton- or photon-based definitive (chemo)radiation or adjuvant (chemo)radiation following Transoral Robotic Surgery. All patients received SAVER enCTV and the primary endpoint was two-year elective out-of-field contralateral nodal failure. Dosimetric comparison between SAVER enCTV and consensus enCTV of the first 10 definitive and adjuvant patients was performed. Overall survival (OS), progression-free-survival (PFS), toxicities, and patient reported outcomes were analyzed. Fifty-two patients were enrolled, of which 36 (69.2%) received definitive (chemo)radiation. Thirty-five (67.3%) had bulky or multiple ipsilateral lymph nodes and 18 (34.6%) had significant smoking history. With median follow-up of 31.0 months (range 13 - 49 months), there were no contralateral nodal failures with an upper limit one-sided 95% confidence interval for contralateral nodal failure of 2.7%. Two-year OS and PFS were 92.2% (95% CI [88.5 - 95.9%]) and 86.2% (95% CI [81.4 - 91.0%]), respectively. Dosimetric comparison demonstrated decreased mean dose (18.3 Gy to 14.1 Gy [p=0.001]) and V30 Gy (20.8% to 11.6% [p=0.003]) to the contralateral parotid with SAVER enCTV. Acute grade 3 toxicity was observed in 13 (25%) patients including 8 (15.4%) who received a gastrostomy tube. There were no grade 4-5 toxicities. Selective avoidance of nodal volumes at minimal risk in the N0 contralateral neck can be safely performed while maintaining excellent regional control in the definitive and adjuvant settings. Dose to contralateral organs at risk and toxicity outcomes were favorable.

papers.abstract: Oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is increasingly encountered in clinical practice, owing to advances in imaging techniques and the emergence of new therapeutic options. This manuscript presents the outcomes of a meeting of experts from Hong Kong, convened to review the evidence and provide guidance on the use of local ablative therapies (LATs) for patients with oligometastatic NSCLC harboring actionable mutations. The discussion addressed key topics, including the definitions of oligometastatic and oligoprogressive disease, criteria for selecting patients for radiotherapy and other LAT modalities, optimal radiotherapy dosage, and the sequencing and timing of LATs in conjunction with targeted molecular therapies. Guidance was also developed regarding whether to pause or continue systemic treatments during LAT, and the evidence supporting emerging biomarkers in this context was reviewed. Consensus statements were formulated using a modified Delphi approach, and several case examples were presented to illustrate the application of these recommendations in clinical management. The consensus statements from this meeting could provide an important basis for tailoring treatment for patients with NSCLC who have actionable mutations, as well as pointing out key areas to explore in upcoming research.

papers.abstract: Patients with mental health disorders prior to cancer diagnosis often present with more advanced-stage cancer compared to those without. Barriers to healthcare access for patients with mental health disorders may have contributed to the observation. The U.S. Military Health System (MHS) is a healthcare system with universal access eligibility among its beneficiary population. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between pre-existing mental health disorders and diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) in the MHS population. The study utilized the Military Cancer Epidemiology database (MilCanEpi), a linked database comprising data from the Department of War's Central Cancer Registry (CCR) and the Military Health System (MHS) Data Repository (MDR). Multinomial logistic regression was used to assess the associations between NHL stage at diagnosis and pre-existing mental health disorders and estimate the odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs). The study included a total of 3498 NHL patients, among them, 644 patients were classified as having mental health disorder diagnoses prior to their NHL diagnosis. There was no association between mental health disorders and NHL stage at diagnosis overall. The adjusted OR for any mental health disorders and a late-stage diagnosis was 0.98 (95% CI=0.79-1.21), and the adjusted OR for an unknown stage diagnosis was 0.91 (95% CI=0.69-1.20). Lack of an association with late stage was also observed in analysis stratified by age, sex, or comorbidities. No association was observed between specific mental health disorder types and NHL stage at diagnosis. Delayed stage at diagnosis of cancer among patients with mental health disorders, shown in the U.S. general population, was not observed for NHL in the MHS system, suggesting the beneficial role of a healthcare system with universal eligibility on NHL diagnosis among patients with mental health disorders.

papers.abstract: Hepatobiliary cancers include hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC), extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ECC), and gallbladder cancer (GBC). We aimed to assess incidence, mortality, survival, and premature mortality of hepatobiliary cancers by subtype in China and progress toward Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) target 3.4. We conducted a nationwide population-based study using data on hepatobiliary cancer cases from 919 cancer registries in China, covering 44.9% of the national population. We estimated incidence, mortality, and premature mortality for 2024 using subtype distributions of HCC, ICC, ECC, and GBC. We quantified 2010-2019 trends using average annual percent changes (AAPCs). Age-standardized 5-year relative survival was estimated using data from 281 registries. Linear trend projections were applied to assess whether current trajectories are sufficient to meet SDG target. In 2024, an estimated 387,600 hepatobiliary cancer cases and 329,500 deaths occurred in China. Age-standardized incidence, mortality, and premature mortality declined, whereas overall 5-year relative survival remained stable at 14.8%. HCC showed sustained declines in incidence, mortality, and premature mortality. ICC incidence increased by 2.4% annually, while ECC mortality and premature mortality rose by 1.6% and 2.8% per year, respectively. HCC was the only subtype with improved survival and was projected to meet the SDG 3.4 premature mortality target by 2030. The disease burden of hepatobiliary cancers remains high in China. Rising ICC and ECC burdens underscore the need to shift from a predominantly HCC-focused approach toward subtype-specific, risk-targeted interventions.

papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is an aggressive malignancy lacking targeted therapies. By screening 200 NPC specimens, we identify homozygous deletion of methylthioadenosine phosphorylase (MTAP) in 37.5% (75/200) of cases, ranking NPC as the second most common cancer type harboring MTAP loss. To target this therapeutic vulnerability, we develop an orally bioavailable methionine adenosyltransferase 2α (MAT2A) inhibitor, BT-115386, which significantly suppresses tumor growth and prolongs survival in mouse models of MTAP-deleted NPC. In MTAP-deleted NPC, BT-115386 treatment reduces protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) activity, thereby enhancing p53 activity through aberrant splicing of MDM4 and inducing c-Myc degradation through abolishment of arginine symmetric dimethylation. Loss of c-Myc thus reduces stemness and lipogenesis but induces cellular differentiation and EBV lytic cycle, indicating that BT-115386 causes MTAP-deleted NPC cell death through multiple pathways. Pharmacological inhibition of MAT2A/PRMT5 is a promising precision therapeutic strategy for MTAP-deficient NPC.

papers.abstract: The cellular origin, clinical significance, and metabolic features of the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) in prostate cancer remain poorly resolved. We integrated bulk transcriptomes from TCGA-PRAD (primary, n = 495) and SU2C (mCRPC, n = 208), two single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets, seven Visium sections, and one Xenium prostate adenocarcinoma section, together with immunoblotting in LNCaP and castration-adapted C4-2 cells treated with charcoal-stripped serum (CSS), enzalutamide (ENZ), and dihydrotestosterone (DHT). SASP formed a smooth, continuous gradient across bulk tumors rather than discrete subtypes. In Xenium, 4,657 of 25,517 tumor cells (18.3%) were positive for a senescence surrogate driven predominantly by p21 (CDKN1A) transcript detection; the local fraction of these cells correlated with a bin-level matrix-remodeling SASP program and glycolysis, but not with inflammatory SASP. The single-cell atlas revealed expansion of AR-low, stasis/senescence-like states in advanced disease. Within the adenocarcinoma compartment of one CRPC section, senescence-like hotspots showed higher glycolysis scores without a concomitant rise in proliferation. In vitro, CSS and ENZ increased p21/p16 and glycolytic proteins (GLUT1, LDHA, HK2), and treatment with 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-DG) or the LDHA inhibitor FX-11 was associated with lower p21/p16 abundance. Androgen deprivation is associated with a prostate cancer senescence-like state and a glycolysis-related program; LDHA is a candidate metabolic node for further investigation; the present data do not establish therapeutic selectivity or efficacy. These spatial associations do not establish the cellular source of the SASP-related transcripts or paracrine signaling.

papers.abstract: Anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy can induce durable remission in patients with large B cell lymphoma (LBCL), yet outcomes remain variable. Reliable pre-treatment predictors of durable response remain limited, leaving a critical gap in patient management. To address this, we profile pre-treatment plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA) from 91 LBCL patients treated with axicabtagene ciloleucel. We demonstrate that signatures of "lymph node-like" tumor microenvironments (TMEs), previously identified in tumor biopsies and shown to correlate with favorable outcomes, are elevated in the pre-treatment plasma cfRNA of responders, but not in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Using unbiased approaches, we identify additional cfRNA signatures associated with 1-year clinical outcomes that capture the underlying biological landscape of treatment response. Collectively, these findings support that pre-treatment plasma cfRNA could serve as a minimally invasive surrogate of TME state to potentially inform CAR T cell therapy outcomes and support risk stratification and TME-modulating adjunct therapies.

papers.abstract: The prevalence of obesity is rising. Patients with obesity are increasingly exposed to anaesthesia, critical care, and perioperative pharmacotherapy. Obesity alters drug pharmacokinetics in a non-linear, drug-specific manner, so that simply scaling doses to total body weight (TBW) exposes patients to overdose or underdose. A recurring clinical question is therefore: which body weight descriptor should be used for which molecule? This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews. We synthesized pharmacokinetic evidence, recent meta-analyses, and French and European guidelines on dose adjustment in adults with obesity for five drug classes of anaesthesia and critical care: hypnotics, opioids, neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBA), perioperative antibiotics, and non-opioid analgesics. We summarised the recommended dosing weight for each molecule in a table and a figure. No single weight descriptor applies. Lipophilic induction agents (propofol), most opioids (alfentanil, fentanyl, sufentanil), and non-depolarising NMBA are best dosed on lean or ideal body weight, whereas succinylcholine, neuromuscular reversal, and aminoglycosides use total or adjusted body weight. Maintenance of hypnosis and pain management in the post-anaesthesia care unit are titrated to monitored effect. Cephalosporin-based antibiotic prophylaxis relies on fixed doses (e.g., cefazolin 2 g) up to high body mass index values due to their hydrophilic properties. Paracetamol and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs are given at standard doses and never scaled to TBW. Findings are consolidated in a single bedside reference table. Dosing in obesity must be molecule-specific, guided by the relevant weight descriptor and by intraoperative monitoring rather than by TBW alone.

papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) may develop through the conventional adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence or alternative routes of carcinogenesis, accompanied by changes in epithelial cell states and remodeling of the tumor microenvironment, yet its core driving mechanisms and therapeutic options remain unclear. This study integrated single-cell, bulk transcriptomic, and spatial transcriptomic datasets for comprehensive bioinformatics analyses, followed by validation in CRC cells and clinical samples using immunohistochemistry. Epithelial cells showed the most pronounced transcriptional and cell-communication remodeling during adenoma-to-carcinoma progression, with marked expansion of tumor-related subpopulations including tumor epithelial cells, stem-like tumor cells, and proliferating tumor cells. Multi-omics integration identified tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 1 (TIMP1) and claudin-23 (CLDN23) as core genes closely linked to inflammatory, immune, and metabolic pathways. Ruxolitinib was predicted to target the TIMP1/CLDN23 regulatory network, and in vitro experiments confirmed that it downregulated TIMP1, upregulated CLDN23, and suppressed CRC cell proliferation. Functional assays further showed that TIMP1 promoted while CLDN23 inhibited CRC cell proliferation and migration, and that the two genes may act cooperatively through their shared downstream molecule selenium-binding protein 1 (SELENBP1). These findings suggest an epithelial-centered mechanism of adenoma-to-CRC progression, identify TIMP1 and CLDN23 as molecules with diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic potential, and provide preliminary support for repurposing Ruxolitinib in CRC.

papers.abstract: The prognostic performance of the Simplified Acute Physiology Score (SAPS) models has not been thoroughly investigated. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed SAPS mortality prediction metrics across diverse intensive care unit (ICU) populations worldwide. PubMed and Scopus were queried for external validations of SAPS in ICU settings. The "CHARMS" and "PROBAST" tools were applied for data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment, respectively. C-statistics and observed-to-expected ratios were summarised using random-effects models. Heterogeneity sources were explored using meta-regression. Evidence certainty was evaluated using the "GRADE" approach. PROSPERO registration CRD42023446721. Ninety studies (89 articles) were reviewed, totalling 565,994 ICU patients across 87 countries, and validating the SAPS II (n = 35), SAPS 3 global (n = 37), and/or SAPS 3 region-specific (n = 28) models. Endpoints were in-hospital (n = 70), in-ICU (n = 16), and/or 28/30-day mortality (n = 12). Nine studies performed recalibrations of SAPS II and 7 of SAPS 3. The meta-analyses provided high-certainty evidence of excellent discriminatory ability across all SAPS models in predicting in-hospital mortality, whereas data on unsatisfactory overall calibration were graded as low certainty. Successful recalibration was graded as high certainty for SAPS II and moderate certainty for SAPS 3. For ICU and 28/30-day mortality, the evidence was low to very low certainty for all SAPS models. Five decision curve analyses were conducted in three studies, all yielding positive net benefit across meaningful risk thresholds. SAPS models remain reliable as mortality risk-ranking tools in critical care. With adequate sample sizes, local recalibrations and dynamic updating of in-hospital mortality predictions are essential to ensure clinical utility. PROSPERO CRD42023446721.

papers.abstract: To update the evidence on neurological and respiratory predictors of extubation failure after acute brain injury and to compare the two families, as pre-specified. Five databases were searched through July 2026 for studies relating a predictor measured at or near extubation to extubation failure in ventilated adults with acute brain injury. Screening and extraction were done in duplicate; risk of bias was assessed using QUIPS. Adjusted estimates were pooled after harmonising outcome framing and predictor coding, restricting each pool to one scale and instrument, with random-effects (REML, Hartung-Knapp) and Bayesian hierarchical models. Certainty was assessed using GRADE. 98 studies (24 505 patients) yielded 415 predictor-outcome estimates; 194 carried a confidence interval, and 6 studies contributed to pooled adjusted estimates. Absent or weak cough was associated with failure (4 studies; OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.46-4.19; posterior median 2.55, 95% CrI 1.54-4.71, P(OR > 1) = 0.999; I² = 0%; moderate certainty), in line with the previous synthesis; in an illustrative projection at a 19% failure rate, about 30% versus 15%. Below-threshold motor GCS was associated with failure in two concordant studies (posterior median OR 5.99, 2.42-16.1; very low certainty). The pre-specified comparison between families could not be validly estimated from published data. An absent or weak cough at extubation is the best-supported single bedside predictor of failure after acute brain injury and should be assessed with secretions, swallowing and consciousness. Fewer than one in ten eligible studies are poolable, mainly for remediable reporting reasons; a minimum reporting set is proposed. PROSPERO CRD420261442541 (submitted 6 July 2026; registered 2 September 2026). Protocol v2.3 was prepared before the searches; the PROSPERO amendment and all deviations are listed in Supplementary Table S1. PRISMA 2020 [1].

papers.abstract: Prophylactic norepinephrine infusion has gained increasing attention to prevent intraoperative hypotension during major non-cardiac surgery, but its effect on haemodynamic stability, tissue perfusion, fluid administration, and postoperative outcomes remains uncertain. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched through May 9, 2026 for randomised trials comparing prophylactic norepinephrine with standard reactive management. Outcomes included change in serum lactate, haemodynamic measures, fluid administration, and postoperative outcomes, including complications and mortality. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, respectively. Sensitivity analyses and trial sequential analysis (TSA) were performed. Eleven trials (1688 patients) were included. Prophylactic norepinephrine was associated with a lower rise in lactate (mean difference (MD) -0.13 mmol/L, 95% CI -0.25 to -0.01; P = 0.03; I²=67.2%), higher post-induction mean arterial pressure (MD 10.79 mmHg, 95% CI 5.53 to 16.04; P < 0.01; I²=95.3%), higher postoperative mean arterial pressure (MD 2.78 mmHg, 95% CI 0.63 to 4.92; P = 0.01; I²=69.8%). Prophylactic norepinephrine use was associated with lower crystalloid administration (MD-548.22 mL, 95% CI -1087.16 to -9.28, P = 0.05, I²=99%) although substantial heterogeneity and protocol-driven differences limit interpretation. Exploratory analyses suggested lower incidences of myocardial infarction (RR 0.25, 95% CI 0.06-0.98), pneumonia (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.36-0.95), and 30 day-surgical site infection (RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.41-0.97). No statistically significant differences were demonstrated for acute kidney injury, atelectasis, length of stay, or mortality. Certainty of evidence was low for most outcomes. TSA indicated insufficient evidence to establish a definitive treatment effect. Prophylactic norepinephrine was associated with a statistically significant but small reduction in intraoperative lactate rise, higher post-induction and post-operative mean arterial pressures. Postoperative complication findings remain exploratory and require confirmation in adequately powered randomised trials. PROSPERO (CRD420261345140).

papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the incremental diagnostic value of peritumoral computed tomography (CT) features for predicting the World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology (WHO/ISUP) nuclear grade in small (2-4 cm) clear cell renal cell carcinomas (ccRCCs). This retrospective multicenter study included 415 patients from institution 1 (initial cohort) and 210 from three other institutions (validation cohort) with surgically confirmed 2 to 4 cm ccRCCs. Conventional intra- and peritumoral CT features were analyzed. Radiomics features were extracted from the internal area of the tumor (IAT) and the peritumoral area of the tumor (PAT 5 mm) on corticomedullary phase CT. Two feature sets (IAT, IAT + PAT 5 mm) underwent identical selection to construct Radscores. Four models were developed using multivariable logistic regression to predict low-grade (grades 1-2) ccRCC. Model performance was compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Practical scoring systems were subsequently constructed. Models including peritumoral features performed better. Clinicoradiologic model 2 (intratumoral + peritumoral) outperformed clinicoradiologic model 1 (intratumoral only), with and AUC of 0.826 versus 0.786 (P = 0.013). Combined model 2 (intratumoral and peritumoral + radscore [IAT+PAT 5 mm]) outperformed combined model 1 (intratumoral + Radscore [IAT]), with an AUC of 0.875 versus 0.814 (P < 0.001). The clinicoradiologic score (0-21) showed 92% specificity for low-grade ccRCC at ≤ 12. The combined score (0-26; cutoff ≤ 18) further improved sensitivity and AUC. Results held in the external validation cohort. Peritumoral CT features significantly improve nuclear grade prediction in small ccRCCs. The clinicoradiologic score effectively identifies low-grade tumors, potentially aiding active surveillance decisions for 2- to 4 cm ccRCCs. Adding radiomics further enhances diagnostic performance.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to assess the association between omission of elective neck dissection (END) and cervical recurrence in patients with cT3/4aN0M0 oral squamous cell carcinoma initially that was downstaged to ycT0-2N0 after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy. This single-center retrospective cohort emulated a target trial involving patients treated during June 2019 to December 2024. All the patients underwent curative-intent primary tumor resection with or without synchronous END. Propensity-score overlap-weighting balanced measured covariates. The primary outcome was 3-year cumulative incidence of cervical recurrence, with death treated as a competing event. Weighted Aalen-Johansen, Fine-Gray, and cause-specific Cox analyses were performed. Among 421 patients, 333 underwent END and 88 had END omitted. The weighted 3-year cumulative incidence of cervical recurrence was 7.2 % versus 14.8 %, respectively (adjusted risk difference, 7.6 percentage points; 95 % CI, -0.8 to 16.0). Omission was associated with higher recurrence rate (subdistribution hazard ratio [HR], 2.06; 95 % confidence interval [CI], 1.03-4.12; cause-specific HR, 2.13; 95 % CI, 1.05-4.33). Although the absolute-effect CI included no difference, clinically important excess recurrence remained possible. These findings do not support routine omission. Among the 333 patients undergoing END, 45 had occult ypN-positive disease (13.5 %; 95 % CI, 10.3 %-17.6 %), and three additional patients had isolated tumor cells only. Among the 45 ypN-positive patients, 36 (80.0 %) had macrometastasis and 6 (13.3 %) had extranodal extension. Of 44 patients with cervical recurrence during complete follow-up evaluation, 34 underwent salvage dissection, and 22 of 30 evaluable patients achieved successful 12-month salvage. Radiologic nodal negativity after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy did not exclude residual disease. Despite uncertainty in the absolute effect, these observational findings do not support routine END omission.

papers.abstract: Chromosomal instability (CIN) is a hallmark of cancer that drives tumor evolution. Recent studies suggest that CIN contributes to cancer cell dissemination and metastasis formation. Here, we assessed this relationship in a panel of human cancer cell lines. Single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based allele-specific copy number analysis was used to determine the weighted genome instability index (wGII) as a measure of CIN in 24 cancer cell lines. Immunofluorescence microscopy was performed to assess micronucleus (MN) formation, cGAS activity, RelB activity, and mitotic chromosome missegregation. Western blotting was employed to analyze for epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT). We established a comprehensive panel of 24 cancer cell lines across four tumor entities (colorectal, lung, pancreatic, and prostate cancer) with a wide metastatic potential spectrum to systematically investigate the role of CIN in metastasis. Although CIN and whole-genome doubling (WGD) were highly prevalent, the wGII did not correlate with mitotic chromosome missegregation rates, MN formation, cGAS-STING signaling, or metastatic potential score of the analyzed cell line panel. Furthermore, neither activation of non-canonical NF-κB signaling nor our EMT-marker based score was associated with increased metastatic potential, indicating that these parameters do not predict metastatic potential. Our study demonstrates that commonly used parameters of genomic instability and EMT do not correlate with the metastatic potential of well-established human cancer cell lines. Improved methods for the reliable assessment of ongoing CIN in tumor cells and three-dimensional cell culture models might be utilized to further analyze the impact of CIN on tumor invasion and metastasis.

papers.abstract: Since 2008, the German Cancer Society (DKG) has certified gynecological cancer centers to ensure high-quality care with guideline-based quality indicators (QI) as a core component. This article summarizes the German development and update of ovarian cancer (OC) QI based on the current S3-guideline (2026) and presents their performance. This was a retrospective, descriptive, observational analysis of aggregated annual-report data for treatment years 2019-2024; no inferential statistics were performed. QI were derived from strong S3-guideline recommendations through a structured multi-step process. Experts identified potential QI according to standardized criteria (including feasibility and impact on care). QI required ≥ 75% agreement. Since 2017, each tumor entity has been limited to five key QI in the certification dataset. Eight guideline-derived QI are currently defined for OC, five QI are included in the certification program. In 2024, 184 certified centers treated 4.951 primary OC cases. At center level, the predefined target values were met for surgical staging (93.5% of centers; target ≥ 40%), offering genetic testing (97.8%; target ≥ 70%), complete macroscopic resection (99.5%; target ≥ 30%), and surgery by a gynecologic oncologist (98.9%; target ≥ 80%). All centers (100%) met plausibility limits for first-line chemotherapy (75.1% of advanced-stage patients). At patient level, pooled adherence rates improved over time; the median rate of offering genetic testing rose from 61% (2019) to 84% (2024). Two QI were retired in 2021, and one QI is pending until further guideline updates. Guideline-based QI translate essential recommendations into measurable metrics, allowing objective assessment of quality. High and increasing adherence rates were observed in certified centers. These findings support the use of guideline-based QI for benchmarking and continuous quality improvement, although the observational design precludes causal attribution to certification.

papers.abstract: Both intrinsic and acquired resistance to poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPis) have emerged as a formidable challenge in clinical practice. Here, we report that the transcription factor E-twenty-six (Ets)-related gene (ERG) was highly expressed in PARPi-resistant prostate cancer and was correlated with PARPi resistance in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) cells. ERG was posttranslationally modified by tripartite motif-containing 28 (TRIM28) as SUMOylation at lysine 389 (K389), which promotes DNA homologous recombination repair (HRR), thereby weakening the efficacy of PARPis. Mechanistically, the SUMOylation of ERG (K389) inhibited protein degradation mediated by the SPOP-mediated ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, thereby stabilizing the protein. Concurrently, this posttranslational modification increased HRR capacity by inhibiting 53BP1 expression, which in turn reduced PARPi sensitivity. Blockade of ERG K389 SUMOylation can effectively impair DNA repair efficacy and overcome PARPi resistance. These findings suggest that TRIM28-mediated ERG SUMOylation conveys resistance to PARPis by inhibiting 53BP1 expression; combined TRIM28/ERG targeting and PARPi therapy may improve outcomes for ERG-positive CRPC patients.
