papers.abstract: RICTOR plays an essential role in regulating mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) kinase activity, but it remains largely elusive how RICTOR is aberrantly activated in human prostate cancer (PrCa). Here, we identify RICTOR as a substrate of Cullin 3-based ubiquitin ligase adaptor SPOP, an important tumor suppressor in PrCa. SPOP deficiency or cancer-derived SPOP mutations disrupt SPOP-mediated degradation of RICTOR, thereby promoting PrCa progression. Furthermore, we identify USP8 as its upstream deubiquitinase, and inhibition of USP8 specifically suppresses RICTOR/mTORC2 activity without affecting mTORC1. As such, the USP8 inhibitor induces RICTOR degradation concomitant with marked tumor suppression in vivo. Hence, these findings reveal an SPOP-USP8-RICTOR regulatory circuit that underlies PrCa tumorigenesis and provides a rationale for targeting RICTOR via USP8 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for patients with PrCa.

papers.abstract: Loss of major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) antigen presentation in tumor cells drives immune evasion and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in colorectal cancer (CRC). To identify therapeutic targets reversing this, we conducted fluorescence-activated cell sorting-based CRISPR activation screens using a druggable genome library and identified folate receptor α (FOLR1) as a top negative regulator. FOLR1 was heterogeneously expressed in CRC tumors but undetectable in adjacent normal tissues. High expression of FOLR1 predicted a poor ICB response, enhanced cancer stemness, and unfavorable patient outcomes. Functional assays showed that FOLR1 promoted CRC stemness-associated properties and fostered an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) with impaired CD8+ T cell infiltration and cytotoxicity, thereby driving tumor progression. Proteomic analyses revealed that FOLR1 stabilized the lactyltransferase AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1), which lactylated signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) at lysine-193 (K193), facilitating its interaction with TCPTP (T cell protein-tyrosine phosphatase) and inducing STAT1 dephosphorylation at tyrosine-701. Consequently, impaired STAT1 signaling down-regulated MHC-I and up-regulated MYC proto-oncogene protein (c-MYC), facilitating evasion of T cell surveillance and enhancing cancer stemness. The anti-FOLR1 antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) mirvetuximab soravtansine (IMGN853) exhibited potent activity against FOLR1-positive CRC cells, reprogramming the TME to an immune-active status. Combining IMGN853 with anti-PD-1 (programmed cell death protein-1) therapy boosted antitumor immunity, sensitized tumors to immunotherapy, and induced robust tumor regression in vivo. Our findings support anti-FOLR1 ADC as a clinically actionable approach to overcome immune evasion and unlock immunotherapy efficacy in CRC.

papers.abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of disease-related death in children, yet effective treatment remains a major clinical challenge. These aggressive tumors have limited therapeutic options capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and frequently recur due to genetic or epigenetic alterations and treatment resistance. Gene therapy offers a promising strategy to address these limitations by modifying gene expression, correcting mutations, or introducing functional genes. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems facilitate this approach by protecting genetic cargo and enabling BBB penetration and tumor-specific uptake. This review summarizes current genetic engineering strategies and NP-based delivery systems for pediatric brain tumors, including their design principles and delivery mechanisms, highlights key therapeutic approaches under preclinical and clinical investigations, and discusses the major challenges and future directions in NP-mediated gene therapy for pediatric neuro-oncology. By critically evaluating these developments, we aim to underscore the transformative potential of NP-mediated gene therapies in reshaping treatment paradigms and improving outcomes and quality of life for children.

papers.abstract: The hypoxic characteristics of the tumor microenvironment and endogenous antioxidant defenses compromise the efficacy of oxygen-consuming oxidative therapy, positioning oxygen-free reductive stress as a new paradigm in tumor treatment. Nevertheless, the immunosuppressive characteristics of hypoxia and reductive stress pose significant challenges for advancing reductive stress-induced immunotherapy. Here, we constructed a hydrogen radical (H•) generator synergistically activated by near-infrared light and thiols, and first elucidated that photocatalytic H•-mediated reductive stress can elicit a robust antitumor immune response via the H•-featured mechanism. Nanoplatform HA@UFTL was engineered using lactate oxidase as an ideal H• partner, with the synergistic contribution enabling cross-amplified antitumor immunotherapy. The H•-participating spatiotemporal sequential strategy highlights a triple spatiotemporal sequential cascade, including dual sequential hypoxia exacerbation, sequential oxidative-reductive stress, and sequential organelle damage. By aggravating rather than alleviating hypoxia, HA@UFTL overcomes immunosuppression induced by hypoxia and reductive stress with H• as a universal building block, providing new insights for hypoxia-based immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Bioorthogonal prodrug activation offers a promising approach for site-specific drug release, significantly reducing the systemic toxicity associated with conventional chemotherapy. However, challenges remain in precisely controlling prodrug activation at the target site while maintaining optimal selectivity, reactivity, and potency. Here, we report a dual-targeting peptide, TzFFYpHH, that integrates on-membrane enzyme-instructed self-assembly (EISA) with bioorthogonal chemistry to enable selective chemotherapy. Exploiting the overexpression of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) on cancer cells, TzFFYpHH selectively anchors and self-assembles on the cancer cell membrane, enriching tetrazine (Tz) handles that act as bioorthogonal reactors to activate a trans-cyclooctene (TCO)-caged prodrug (TCO-Dox) for precise drug release. Upon topical administration, TzFFYpHH forms a hydrogel at subcutaneous tumor sites, enabling in situ prodrug activation for effective tumor inhibition. Notably, this localized chemotherapy elicits a potent antitumor immune response, which, when combined with anti-programmed death-1 antibody (αPD-1), synergistically potentiates therapeutic outcomes. By coupling supramolecular self-assembly with bioorthogonal reactivity on the cell membrane, this work establishes a chemically programmable platform for spatiotemporally controlled prodrug activation and provides a general strategy for integrating localized chemotherapy with immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS) is an immune disorder characterized by defective lymphocyte apoptosis, leading to lymphoproliferation, autoimmunity, and increased lymphoma risk. Although disease severity correlates with the expansion of double-negative T (DNT) cells, the mechanisms governing their aberrant generation and pathogenicity remain elusive. Through single-cell transcriptomics of peripheral blood from pediatric patients with ALPS, including patients harboring new FAS cell surface death receptor (FAS) mutations (FAS mutations), we identified a pathogenic effector DNT subset (GRANZYMEhiCXCR5hi) exhibiting cytotoxic and tissue-infiltrating features, a population conserved in ALPS mouse models. Using an apoptosis-defective murine model that develops early-onset ALPS with robust DNT cell expansion, we found that ALPS-associated caspase-8 functional impairment facilitates receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1) activation to drive disease pathogenesis, a process exacerbated by receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 3 (RIPK3) scaffold function. Peripheral CD8+ T cells from both patients with ALPS and mouse models exhibited increased susceptibility to activation-induced conversion into pathogenic DNT cells, which was effectively blocked by RIPK1 inhibition. Mechanistically, RIPK1 activation drove peripheral CD8+ T cells to adopt a pathogenic DNT fate via cAMP-responsive element modulator (CREM)-mediated CD8 silencing. Furthermore, genetic or pharmacological inhibition of RIPK1 kinase activity reduced DNT cell generation and burden in target organs, reversed cytopenias, and alleviated autoimmune pathology in ALPS mouse models. Our findings establish RIPK1 as a critical driver of ALPS pathogenesis and identify RIPK1 inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. papers.abstract: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy (CART) is a life-saving regimen for children with relapsed/refractory (r/r) B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL), yet children from lower socioeconomic and historically marginalized backgrounds are less likely to receive it. Understanding the provider experience of CART referral and post-CART clinical management is critical for designing effective interventions to improve access. To explore physicians' experiences identifying and referring pediatric patients with r/r B-ALL for CART across diverse hospital settings, and to identify physician-perceived facilitators and barriers to CART treatment. Focus groups using a semi-structured guide were conducted with pediatric oncology physicians, recruited via email and at a national conference, with targeted recruitment of National Cancer Institute Community Oncology Research Program (NCORP) site providers. Questions explored identifying pediatric patients with r/r B-ALL as CART candidates, referring them for CART, and accessing institutional infrastructure to support referral. Analysis revealed six domains spanning referral to CART and subsequent CART treatment: identification of potentially eligible patients; complexity of CART referral; barriers to insurance approval; physician perception of patients' social/financial circumstances; and variability in pre- and post-CART management guidelines. Health system-level facilitators and barriers included patient identification and referral processes to tertiary care centers, guidelines for bridging therapy and post-CART toxicity management, and navigation support for patient care and insurance approval. Findings highlight challenges in community-based settings where resources, infrastructure and geographic availability for CART are variable. Standardizing referral pathways, centralizing trial information, and streamlining CART-center intake process and communication are of immediate importance.

papers.abstract: This multicenter case-control study assessed (2019-2023) the association of oral and anogenital human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes with head and neck cancers in Brazil. Eligible cases were adults (≥ 18 years) with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx. Controls (cancer-free individuals) were matched a posteriori by region, sex, and age. Oral, genital, and anal samples were collected and processed at a central laboratory for HPV genotyping. Associations were estimated using conditional regression. Analyses included 314 participants (157 cases, 157 controls), mostly males (79%) aged 50-65 years (51%). Oral HPV prevalence was similar between cases and controls (14% vs. 12%), predominantly involving high-risk genotypes (35 out of 40); HPV-16/18 was more prevalent among cases (7.3% vs. 1.9%; p = 0.024), with most HPV-16/18-positive cancers located in the oropharynx (10 out of 11). Genital HPV prevalence was 39% with no case-control differences, while anal HPV prevalence was 17%. Cases were more frequently positive for any high-risk anal HPV type than controls (16% vs. 9%; p = 0.049). Minimal genotype concordance was observed between oral and anogenital sites. Current smokers had ten-fold higher odds of being cases (adjustedOR 10.0; 95% CI 2.92-34.6). Oral HPV-16/18 infection was independently associated with head and neck cancer (adjustedOR 6.30; 95% CI 1.52-26.1). Multisite HPV genotyping revealed site-specific colonization patterns, with genital infections being most prevalent among both men and women. After multivariable adjustment, only oral HPV-16/18 infection was strongly associated with head and neck cancer, especially oropharyngeal carcinoma.

papers.abstract: Breast stroma may play an important role in carcinogenesis. We examined the associations of stromal markers alpha-smooth muscle actin (αSMA), tenascin-C (TNC), fibroblast activation protein (FAP), calcyclin (s100a6), and matrix metallo-proteinase (MMP14) in benign breast biopsy samples with subsequent breast cancer (BCa) risk. This study included women with biopsy-confirmed benign breast disease (BBD) from a nested case-control study within the Nurses' Health Study (NHS) and NHSII cohorts. The data on BCa risk factors were obtained from questionnaires updated biennially. Multiplex immunofluorescence (IF) of stromal markers was completed on tissue microarrays. For each core, the percent (%) positivity was quantified using inForm v2.6.0. Multivariate logistic regression was used to examine the associations of each marker's expression (continuous and binary with 1% cutoff) with BCa risk, while adjusting for BCa risk factors. Among the 370 women (82 cases/288 controls), 106 (28.7%) had non-proliferative BBD, 205 (55.4%) had proliferative BBD without atypia, and 59 (16.0%) had proliferative BBD with atypia. We found suggestive evidence of positive associations of FAP expression with BCa cancer risk (OR per 10% change in expression = 1.15, 95% CI: 0.98-1.35). The expression of αSMA, s100a6, TNC, and MMP14 was not associated with subsequent BCa risk. In secondary models adjusting for BBD subtype and % mammographic breast density, these results remained similar. Our findings suggest that increased stromal fibroblast activation (as captured by FAP expression) may be associated with greater subsequent BCa risk. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.abstract: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a frequent complication of advanced cancers and is associated with poor prognosis, including in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). We characterized T-cell populations in pleural effusion samples from patients with malignant (n = 34) and benign (n = 11) conditions using multiparametric flow cytometry and cytokine analysis, complemented by reanalysis of publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing datasets. MPE was characterized by enrichment of CD8⁺ effector memory (EM) T cells, including a distinct EOMEShighPD-1highCD103+ population. This subset exhibited increased expression of tissue residency-associated markers, including CD69 and CXCR6, together with increased granzyme B and Ki-67 expression and enhanced IFN-γ production following CD3/CD28 stimulation. Despite high PD-1 expression, it did not exhibit a coordinated increase in exhaustion-associated markers. Single-cell transcriptomic analyzes of breast cancer- and lung adenocarcinoma-associated MPE datasets identified related HLA-II⁺ CD8⁺ T-cell states with effector-associated features, and increased HLA-DR protein expression was confirmed by flow cytometry. Among patients receiving ICIs, this population was more abundant in those showing improvement in malignant pleural effusion, whose overall responses ranged from stable disease to partial response, whereas patients without pleural effusion improvement had progressive disease. These findings identify a tissue residency-associated, HLA-II-expressing CD8⁺ EM T-cell population with effector-associated features in MPE and suggest its potential clinical relevance during ICI therapy.

papers.abstract: AMP-410 achieves potent antitumor efficacy with high therapeutic index and favorable tolerability in murine tumor models. It is a conditional bifunctional VEGF-4-1BB biologic designed to simultaneously neutralize VEGF and activate 4-1BB signaling, delivering a localized and dual-action approach to immunotherapy. By leveraging VEGF-dependent activation of 4-1BB, AMP-410 preferentially enhances immune responses within the tumor microenvironment, minimizing systemic toxicity while amplifying innate and adaptive immunity. In human 4-1BB transgenic mice bearing syngeneic tumors (MC38 colorectal carcinoma and B16F10 melanoma), AMP-410 promoted rapid M1 macrophage differentiation and enhanced progenitor-exhausted (Pex) T-cell signatures, suggesting coordinated activation of innate and adaptive compartments. At later stages, AMP-410 sustained macrophage antitumor activity and a continued expansion of Pex cells, consistent with long-term immune engagement. Localized activity was indicated by clonal T-cell expansion within tumors with minimal draining lymph node exchange. Compared with the systemic 4-1BB agonist urelumab in syngeneic tumor models, AMP-410 provided superior long-term protection with reduced exhaustion and improved hepatic tolerability. In head-to-head testing against a VEGF-PD-1 bispecific, AMP-410 achieved robust tumor suppression and survival benefits without systemic IFNγ surges. To establish translational relevance, VEGF concentrations were measured in tumor interstitial fluid from patients with cancer. VEGF levels were consistently two to four orders of magnitude higher in tumors than in matched serum, supporting the clinical opportunity of VEGF-restricted 4-1BB activation. Together, these studies position AMP-410 as a promising next-generation immunotherapy for both monotherapy and combination settings, with the potential to overcome key limitations of existing checkpoint- and 4-1BB-based approaches. Localizing 4-1BB activity to VEGF-rich tumor microenvironments may expand the therapeutic window of 4-1BB costimulation, promoting strong antitumor immunity while limiting systemic immune activation and liver inflammation.

papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of antibody therapeutics is shifting the clinical bottleneck from drug availability to precise patient selection. We systematically characterize 87 clinically actionable tumor-associated antigens across solid tumors by integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, spatial, and single-cell profiles from more than 32,000 specimens to define expression prevalence, intratumoral heterogeneity, immune contexture, internalization and payload-sensitivity pathways, and translational relevance. We establish ANCHOR, a coordinate reference framework for standardizing patient RNA-seq data, and develop ReSort, a two-tiered scoring system for scalable target prioritization. ReSort enables virtual basket and umbrella trial matching, demonstrates concordance with clinical assays, predicts therapeutic response in patient-derived models, and identifies repurposing opportunities in rare malignancies. We develop an AI-based decision-support agent for antibody trial matching and construct a multimodal feature space integrating tumor- and protein-intrinsic attributes to guide systematic target discovery and prioritization. This work provides a scalable, clinically actionable approach for precision antibody-based therapies and next-generation target development.

papers.abstract: Given that CD19 chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell therapy frequently induces severe thrombocytopenia and recombinant human thrombopoietin (rhTPO)'s role in managing this CAR-T-associated cytopenia remains not well defined, we aimed to evaluate rhTPO's safety and efficacy for treating thrombocytopenia in B-cell malignancy patients after tandem dual-target (CD19/20 or CD19/22) CAR-T therapy. A multicenter retrospective study (2018-2024) enrolled 53 patients. rhTPO was administered for platelets < 50 × 109/L or bleeding risk; platelet counts were monitored for 4 weeks post-treatment initiation. rhTPO was initiated pre/post-CAR-T (median 7 days post-infusion, 13-day duration). Baseline platelets (25 × 109/L) rose to 25, 26, 48 × 109/L at 7, 14, 28 days post-rhTPO. Of 38 transfusion-requiring patients, 71.1% achieved ≥ 20 × 109/L without transfusion by day 28. rhTPO did not affect CAR-T expansion. Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) occurred in 77.4% (17.0% grade ≥ 3), immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) in 13.2% (all grade 1), and the 30-day infection rate was 41.5%; no rhTPO-related toxicities were observed. rhTPO effectively manages peri-CAR-T thrombocytopenia in B-cell malignancy patients, with no elevated risks of CRS, ICANS, or infections.

papers.abstract: Delays in Breast Cancer diagnosis and treatment remain common in low and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet evidence on the effectiveness and sustainability of quality improvement (QI) initiatives in resource-constrained cancer centers is limited. We prospectively evaluated a quality improvement (QI) initiative designed to reduce treatment delays at a national cancer center in Mexico and assessed the sustainment of its effects. We analyzed time intervals for 933 newly diagnosed breast cancer patients presenting between September 2023 and December 2024 across three phases: pre-intervention, active intervention, and sustainment. The QI initiative was informed by a prior needs assessment and included workflow modifications, systematic monitoring and feedback on time-to-care metrics, and monthly multidisciplinary meetings. Outcomes included median Total Time-to-Treatment (TTT), Time-to-Diagnosis (TTD), Time-to-Tumor Board (TTB), and Time-from-Diagnosis-to-Treatment (TDT). Median TTT decreased from 51 days at baseline to 43 days during the intervention phase (p < 0.001) but returned to 51 days during sustainment. TTB showed consistent improvement, decreasing from 34 days at baseline to 28 days during the intervention and remained shorter during sustainment (27 days, p < 0.001 vs. baseline). TTD did not improve during active implementation but decreased during sustainment (19 days, p < 0.001). TDT did not change significantly during the intervention (26 vs. 22 days) but increased to 30 days during sustainment (p < 0.001 vs. intervention). Monthly patient volume increased by 24.1% between the baseline and sustainment periods, coinciding with the loss of overall TTT improvement. This low-cost QI initiative produced meaningful reductions in BC treatment delays and achieved sustained improvements in Time-to-Tumor Board. However, gains in overall treatment timeliness were not sustained as patient volume and external system pressures exceeded institutional capacity. These findings underscore both the potential and limitations of workflow-focused QI initiatives in resource-constrained cancer centers and underscore the importance of evaluating sustainment alongside short-term effectiveness.

papers.abstract: Melanoma is the most malignant form of skin cancer. Due to its heterogeneity and aggressiveness, genetic characterization of melanoma primary tumors and/or metastases in advanced AJCC stages of the disease is crucial to find an appropriate therapy. In this study, we investigated genetic profiles of 283 melanoma primary and metastatic site tissue samples of a large cohort of 227 patients using a targeted multigene sequencing-panel. Thereby, paired primary and metastatic site samples of 33 patients were available. The evaluation of paired tissue samples demonstrated divergences in one third of all paired samples even including important driver genes (BRAF/NRAS). In paired samples, additional variants in the metastatic site, but also a loss of pathogenic variants in the metastases were found. Sequencing confirmed the four most frequently altered genes in melanoma: BRAF, NRAS, TP53 and CDKN2A with 38.5%, 24.4%, 19.8% and 11.3%, respectively. When comparing pathogenic variants in primary lesions (n = 125) and metastatic sites (n = 152), these genes showed higher variant frequencies in metastases. Regarding melanoma subtypes, acral cutaneous melanoma showed significantly higher counts of identical variant spectra compared to non-acral melanoma (p-value = 0.012). Results underline the presence of subpopulations within the primary tumor and the occurrence of additional mutational events in disease progression.

papers.abstract: This study aims to investigate the association between dietary inflammatory potential and postoperative health-related quality of life (HRQOL) in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) survivors. A prospective cohort study was conducted to recruit patients undergoing esophagectomy for newly diagnosed ESCC from two hospitals in Fujian Province. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ), and the Energy-adjusted Dietary Inflammatory Index (E-DII) was calculated based on the FFQ. Participants were followed for 7 years, during which HRQOL was monitored 16 times via telephone interview. The time to deterioration (TTD) model was utilized to compute patients' longitudinal changes in HRQOL scores. A total of 376 ESCC patients were included in the study. The results indicated that patients in the pro-inflammatory diet group had a higher incidence of deterioration events in the functional and symptomatic domains. Additionally, they experienced a significantly earlier deterioration in cognitive functioning (median TTD, 20.895 months vs. 34.234 months, p = 0.032) and eating problems (median TTD, 13.864 months vs. 16.756 months, p = 0.026) postoperatively. Both univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses showed that higher E-DII scores were significantly associated with an increased risk of deterioration in cognitive functioning (HR = 1.322, 95% CI: 1.015-1.722) and eating problems (HR = 1.290, 95% CI: 1.010-1.648) among ESCC patients postoperatively. A higher preoperative E-DII score is associated with an increased risk of postoperative HRQOL deterioration among ESCC patients, particularly in the domains of cognitive functioning and eating problems. Our findings offer new insights into dietary interventions and treatment strategies for ESCC survivors.

papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform increasingly well on medical benchmarks, yet benchmark success does not necessarily establish clinical readiness in oncology. Building on recent critiques of medical LLM evaluation, this Perspective identifies four benchmark-practice mismatches: complete-information benchmarks versus active information gathering, single reference answers versus preference-sensitive decisions, cross-sectional snapshots versus longitudinal disease trajectories, and standalone model performance versus model-in-system readiness. To address these gaps, we propose a four-stage evaluation paradigm progressing from a structured knowledge and reasoning baseline to interactive and dialogue-based evaluation, longitudinal trajectory assessment, and model-in-system evaluation. Grounded in the longitudinal, multimodal, and multidisciplinary nature of oncology care, the framework emphasizes the need to calibrate evaluation to intended use and clinical risk and to sustain assessment through continuous monitoring across the model life cycle. Together, these principles offer an operational and oncology-specific pathway for building progressively stronger evidence of clinical readiness.

papers.abstract: Carbon ions have biophysical advantages over photons, including a finite range, increased relative biological effectiveness, and lowered oxygen dependence. Maximum treatment flexibility is attainable with rotational beam delivery. We report our clinical experience using the carbon-ion gantry at the Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center with intensity-controlled raster scanning capability, focusing on treatment toxicity. A total of 1622 patients treated using the carbon-ion gantry between 2012 and 2026 were evaluated. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Toxicity analysis was conducted using Common Terminology Criteria of Adverse Events v5.0. The median age preradiation therapy was 59 years (range, 18-91). Most patients had locally advanced tumors (21.8% T4; 11.2% T3) without regional lymph node metastases (45.4% N0). The most common treatment indications were sacrococcygeal tumors (n = 331; 20.4%), followed by tumors of the paranasal sinuses (n = 166; 10.2%) and the spine (n = 121; 7.5%). A total of 486 patients (30.0%) received carbon-ion reirradiation, the most frequent carbon-ion gantry treatment indication viewed across all patients. The most common particle therapy beam-angle number was 2 (range, 1-7). The use of more than 2 beam angles was particularly frequent in tumors of the skull base (45.8%) and the thoracic region (40.0%). High-grade (III and IV) acute and late toxicity rates were 2.4% and 4.2% in primary treatment. Mean numbers of acute and late grade I and II toxicity events per patient were 2.2 (95% confidence interval, 2.0-2.4) and 2.0 (95% confidence interval, 1.7-2.4), respectively. Carbon-ion radiation therapy using a heavy-ion gantry resulted in favorable toxicity rates in specific indications. Further interdisciplinary research demonstrating the clinical benefit of carbon-ion radiation therapy is required. This study provides more evidence supporting particle therapy facilities and may serve as a foundation for prospective clinical trials.

papers.abstract: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is effectively treated with small molecule BCR::ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) but as in all cancers, early identification of suboptimal responders and non-responders is a challenge. Through mass cytometry analysis of peripheral blood leukocytes collected on the first day of TKI treatment, we generated high-dimensional single-cell data from de novo chronic phase CML patients enrolled in two multicenter clinical trials (clinicaltrials.gov: NCT01725204 and NCT01061177). In leukocytes, dasatinib and nilotinib inhibited intracellular signaling within 1 or 3 h after first oral dose, respectively, and each TKI had a unique signaling signature reflecting its kinase specificity profile beyond BCR::ABL1. From these data, an immune and signaling profile was constructed for each patient that predicted the treatment response (BCR::ABL1IS, %) during the first 12 months of treatment. The predictive features were drug specific: response to dasatinib was dominated by leukemic burden, neutrophil maturity (pSTAT3 Y705) and immune effector activity (pERK ½ in T- and NK cells), whereas response to nilotinib was driven by the intrinsic signaling states of CD34+CD38lowCD25+ LSC-like cells (cleaved caspase-3, pCRKL Y207 and STAT3 [total and Y705]). These results show that single cell immune and signaling profiles measured within hours of first dose can predict 12-month treatment response, anticipating future optimization of kinase inhibitor treatment within days rather than months.

papers.abstract: MnTnBuOE-2-PyP5+ (BMX-001) is a manganese metalloporphyrin superoxide dismutase mimic that inhibits radiation stress-induced pathways and may mitigate treatment-related side effects. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of BMX-001 on severe oral mucositis (OM), xerostomia, dermatitis, quality of life, and patient reported outcomes (PROs) among patients undergoing chemoradiation for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). This multicenter, phase I/II trial included patients with stage III-IVB HNSCC (AJCC 7th ed) undergoing definitive or postoperative chemoradiation (CRT). Patients received a subcutaneous BMX-001 loading dose followed by twice-weekly maintenance dosing through one week post-CRT at three loading/maintenance dose levels (7/3.5 mg, 14/7 mg, and 28/14 mg), with level 3 expanded for phase II endpoints. OM, xerostomia, and dermatitis were assessed weekly during treatment, within one month, and at six and 12 months post-chemoradiation. PROs and saliva production (stimulated and unstimulated) were measured at baseline, end of CRT, and one, six and 12 months post-CRT. Descriptive statistics summarized adverse events, symptom duration, and PROs. Between 5/2017 and 12/2019, 29 patients were enrolled; 86% had oropharynx primaries (n=25; n=24 HPV+) and 89.7% (n=26) underwent definitive CRT. One patient experienced two serious adverse events possibly related to BMX-001. Grade 3 OM occurred in 41.4% (n=12); acute and chronic grade ≥2 xerostomia occurred in 17.9% (n=5) and 9.1% (n=2), respectively, and 6.9% (n=2) experienced grade 3 dermatitis. At a median follow-up of 24 months, 96.6% were alive without progression. In exploratory longitudinal analyses of the 23 patients treated at the recommended phase II dose, patient-reported symptom and quality-of-life measures generally worsened at the end of CRT and subsequently improved. Several measures were no longer statistically different from baseline by six months, while measures of xerostomia remained elevated. BMX-001 is safe and feasible in patients with advanced HNSCC. In addition, BMX-001 shows promising efficacy for mitigating CRT-associated toxicity and warrants further study in larger, controlled trials.

papers.abstract: To characterize immediate breast reconstruction (IBR) utilization and its associations with Affordable Care Act (ACA) era and race among men with breast cancer, with analyses among women to extend prior female-focused research and provide a comparative context. We performed a retrospective analysis of male mastectomy patients in the National Cancer Database (NCDB) from 2005 to 2022, and conducted analyses in the female mastectomy cohort as a comparator. Temporal trends in IBR were evaluated using piecewise logistic regression with a breakpoint at ACA expansion in 2013. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of reconstruction stratified by sex. Among male patients, IBR remained uncommon throughout the study period (3.7%) and was not significantly associated with ACA implementation. In the female patients, IBR utilization increased over time and was significantly higher in the post-ACA era compared with the pre-ACA period (OR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.25-1.27, p < 0.001). Racial disparities in reconstruction were observed among women but were not statistically significant among men, though interpretation is limited by small sample size. Across both sexes, younger age, higher income, earlier disease stage, treatment at integrated cancer programs, and contralateral prophylactic mastectomy were associated with higher odds of reconstruction (p < 0.01). Despite higher reconstruction utilization among women in the post-ACA era, reconstruction among men remained uncommon and no significant association was observed between ACA era and reconstruction utilization among male patients. These findings suggest persistent sex differences in reconstruction utilization and underscore the additional efforts to better understand reconstruction decision-making in this understudied population.

papers.abstract: European LeukemiaNet defines the clinical signs and symptoms (CSSs) of polycythemia vera (PV) as progressive splenomegaly, leukocytosis, thrombocytosis, inadequate hematocrit control, and cardiovascular risk factors. In PV patients receiving hydroxyurea, CSSs indicate a phenotype with higher thrombosis risk across the standard risk categories. However, the prognostic value of CSSs for thrombosis or progression to secondary myelofibrosis (SMF) or acute leukemia (AL) during second-line ruxolitinib therapy remains unknown. We assessed the incidence rate ratios (IRRs) of thrombosis and disease progression during ruxolitinib treatment, and the prognostic impact of CSSs at treatment initiation, in 254 PV patients from the PV-ARC multicenter cohort. CSSs were identified in 50.4% of patients, with similar proportions in low- and high-risk groups (50% vs 50.5%). The IRRs for thrombosis and progression to SMF/AL were 1.0 and 4.2 %p‑y, respectively. Conventional thrombotic risk categories did not predict thrombosis or progression. In contrast, CSSs were associated with higher IRRs of both thrombosis (1.8 vs 0 %p‑y, p = 0.05) and progression (6.0 vs 2.3 %p‑y, p = 0.02). Persistent or progressive leukocytosis was the strongest predictor of disease progression. In conclusion, CSSs refine conventional risk stratification by improving prediction of thrombosis and disease progression during ruxolitinib, supporting their integration into routine clinical assessment.

papers.abstract: Serrated neoplasia represents an increasingly recognized pathway in colorectal carcinogenesis, accounting for up to 30% of colorectal cancers (CRC) and disproportionately implicated in post-colonoscopy CRC. Serrated polyps remain under-detected, incompletely resected, and inconsistently classified histologically, presenting challenges for both non-invasive and colonoscopy-based screening programs. In this comprehensive review, we address advances in the understanding of the serrated pathway, integrating molecular pathways with key histologic classification updates from the 6th edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Digestive Tumor System. We further appraise contemporary evidence regarding the epidemiology and risk factors for serrated polyps, and discuss thresholds for detection via colonoscopy, specifically the sessile serrated lesion detection rate, which is an independent predictor of post-colonoscopy CRC risk. Finally, we address advances in endoscopic detection and resection and synthesize current international surveillance guidelines. With increasing awareness and rising detection benchmarks, a thorough and up to date understanding of the serrated neoplasia is essential for gastroenterologists, pathologists, and primary care providers involved in CRC prevention, in order to reduce its substantial contribution to the burden of CRC worldwide.

papers.abstract: To evaluate the association between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use and overall survival in women with endometrial cancer. Using the TriNetX network, we identified women aged 18-75 years with endometrial cancer diagnosed between 2018 and 2024 and propensity score matched those with a GLP-1RA record within 12 months before diagnosis to women without prior use, with follow-up anchored to the date of diagnosis. A 2-year landmark analysis compared new GLP-1RA use within 2 years of diagnosis with no use among women alive at 2 years without evidence of advanced disease, and sensitivity analyses included an active comparator, race-stratified analyses and a negative-control outcome. The outcome was 5-year all-cause mortality. In the primary analysis (2646 matched pairs), 5-year survival was 91.6% among GLP-1RA users and 90.2% among non-users (hazard ratio [HR] 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65-1.02), and in the 2-year landmark analysis (2275 pairs) it was 96.4% and 96.3% (HR 0.92; 95% CI, 0.63-1.34). Results were similar against dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (HR 0.91; 95% CI, 0.45-1.84) and by race (interaction P = 0.46), whereas a comparison with women who never received a GLP-1RA, as in previous studies, yielded an HR of 0.58 (95% CI, 0.48-0.70). Once follow-up was anchored to the date of diagnosis, GLP-1RA use was not associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality in women with endometrial cancer, and these hypothesis-generating findings should temper the extrapolation of survival associations reported in other cancers until prospective trials are completed.

papers.abstract: Previous studies have shown disparities in cancer outcomes according to the healthcare funding source. Here, we aimed to analyze the overall survival (OS) of patients with cervical cancer treated in the public and private healthcare systems in São Paulo, Brazil. This retrospective cohort study analyzed patients with cervical cancer enrolled in the Registro Hospitalar de Câncer da Fundação Oncocentro de São Paulo (RHC-FOSP) database, with diagnosis between January 2012 and December 2019. The primary objective was to compare OS of patients treated with public versus private healthcare funding. The type of funding source was determined by the healthcare service involved in the initial evaluation and treatment. For descriptive purposes, subgroup analyses considering the age group, educational level, and TNM stage at diagnosis were performed. Of the 21,993 individuals with cervical cancer recorded in the RHC-FOSP database, 11,662 were included in the analysis (10,985 [94.2%] with public healthcare funding; 677 [5.8%] with private funding). Patients in the private system were younger and had higher educational levels than those in the public system. At 5-year follow-up, the median OS was not reached. Private funding was associated with significantly higher OS compared with public funding, with 5-year crude OS rates of 67.3% (95% CI, 63.1-71.8) and 50.4% (95% CI, 49.5-51.4), respectively. After adjusting for age and TNM stage, public funding was still associated with a worse prognosis for patients with more than 8 years of education versus private funding (adjusted HR of 1.36; 95% CI, 1.08-1.72, P = 0.009). Public healthcare funding is significantly associated with a worse OS in patients with cervical cancer in São Paulo, Brazil. These findings highlight the need for policy interventions to improve timely access to optimal cancer care, particularly in the public sector.

papers.abstract: Distant-stage incidence and cancer-specific mortality describe different aspects of cancer burden. We compared their long-term population trends across 10 solid cancers in the United States. Age-adjusted distant-stage incidence from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program 17 Registries database (SEER17) and national cancer-specific mortality were analyzed for 2004-2023 using Joinpoint regression. Primary incidence models omitted 2020; mortality models retained 2020. Both endpoints were also analyzed over a common 2004-2019 window. Endpoint direction was defined from the 95% confidence interval for average annual percentage change (AAPC). Relative survival and incidence-based mortality were complementary analyses. Among 5,545,600 incident cancers, 1,060,790 were diagnosed at distant stage. Breast cancer, prostate cancer, and melanoma had increasing distant-stage incidence with declining mortality; lung and colorectal cancers declined in both endpoints; pancreatic, liver and intrahepatic bile duct, and uterine cancers increased in both; and kidney and renal pelvis and stomach cancers had no clear incidence change with declining mortality. All 10 paired patterns were unchanged in the common 2004-2019 window. One- and 3-year distant-stage relative survival increased for all cancers, and all 20 primary survival contrasts remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. The relation between distant-stage incidence and cancer-specific mortality differed by cancer site and was unchanged in a common pre-pandemic window. Distant-stage incidence is best interpreted alongside, rather than as a substitute for, population mortality.

papers.abstract: Progenitor CD4+ T (Tpex) cells retain developmental plasticity and replenish antigen-specific CD4+ T cell responses in settings of chronic infection and cancer. Given the sustained, elevated expression of the transcription factor TOX across all CD4+ TEX cell subsets during chronic infection, we examined how TOX impacts CD4+ TEX differentiation during chronic infection. Deletion of TOX in lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV)-specific transgenic CD4+ T cells impaired Tpex cell survival and drove unrestrained TEX cell differentiation. Multiomic profiling revealed that this effector-like state was concomitant with loss of TCF-1 pathway activity and gain of NFAT, NF-κB, and RUNX-coordinated transcriptional circuitry. TOX also promoted the multipotent potential of CD4+ Tpex cells to differentiate into T helper (Th)1-like or Tfh-like cells by day 8 post-infection (p.i.) prior to establishment of chronic infection. These data reveal a TOX-driven transcriptional network that maintains CD4+ Tpex cell function and persistence, supporting a durable and malleable response during persisting antigen stimulation.

papers.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are essential redox messengers, yet their effects depend on concentration, localization, and duration. Here, we investigate how compartment-specific hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) production influences cardiomyocyte redox signaling and function. Using human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CM) expressing the H₂O₂ biosensor HyPer fused to D-amino acid oxidase (DAO), we achieve chemogenetic control of H₂O₂ generation in the cytosol, mitochondria, or nucleus. Cytosolic H₂O₂ propagates throughout the cell, whereas mitochondrially generated H₂O₂ remains spatially restricted, reflecting compartmentalized antioxidant buffering. Cytosolic H₂O₂ impairs contractility and relaxation in both 2D and 3D engineered heart tissue models, accompanied by preferential oxidation of Z-disc-associated and actin-binding proteins and by altered sarcomere organization. Antioxidant treatment attenuates these effects. In contrast, mitochondrially produced H₂O₂ is better tolerated and associated with adaptive redox remodeling, with preserved contractile performance that is antagonized by conoidin A-induced inhibition of cytosolic peroxiredoxin activity. These findings demonstrate that the subcellular source of H₂O₂ shapes redox propagation, oxidation patterns, and functional responses, highlighting redox compartmentalization as a determinant of cardiomyocyte performance and stress resilience.

papers.abstract: Identification of partial loss-of-function (hypomorphic), reduced penetrance pathogenic missense variants (RPPVs) and assessment of the clinical relevance of these variants is needed for improved hereditary cancer risk estimation. Here we show that 70 candidate hypomorphic missense variants in the DNA-binding domain of BRCA2 reduce homologous recombination DNA repair activity and endogenous cell survival, decrease RAD51 foci formation, and increase sensitivity to Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors. The 34 "strong" hypomorphs with greatest effects on function are associated with moderate risks of female breast cancer and later ages of diagnosis than pathogenic variants (PVs), and 14 of these variants can be classified as "likely pathogenic" by integration of functional data into a ClinGen BRCA1/2 variant curation model. In addition, 32% of tumors with hypomorphic variants and corresponding loss of heterozygosity for BRCA2 display homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) compared to 83% of tumors with PVs and 7% with benign variants. These RPPVs represent a class of BRCA2 variants that have implications for the clinical management of carriers.

papers.abstract: Cisplatin-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) is the standard for locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). For cisplatin (CDDP)-ineligible patients, mitomycin C/5-fluorouracil (MMC/5-FU) is the most common alternative, but randomized comparisons are lacking. We compared MMC/5-FU with CDDP/5-FU as concurrent partners of hyperfractionated-accelerated radiotherapy (HART) in unresectable, locally advanced HNSCC. In this multicenter phase III trial, 364 patients with stage IVA/IVB (UICC TNM 6th edition) oropharyngeal or hypopharyngeal HNSCC were randomized 1:1 to HART (72 Gy/6 weeks) plus either weekly CDDP 30 mg/m² (n=182) or MMC 10 mg/m² on days 5 and 36 (n=182), both with continuous-infusion 5-FU 600 mg/m²/d on days 1-5. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS); secondary endpoints included freedom from progression (FFP), freedom from distant metastasis (FFDM), local, regional and locoregional control, and toxicity, analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and, post hoc, in a competing-risk framework. After a median follow-up of 87 months, CDDP/5-FU was not superior for OS (10-year OS 23% vs. 18%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.89, 95% CI 0.69-1.15; log-rank p=0.418). In the competing-risk analysis, CDDP/5-FU reduced distant metastasis (5-year cumulative incidence 25.9% vs. 36.1%; subdistribution HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.45-0.96; p=0.031) and progression (45.6% vs. 56.3%; subdistribution HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.55-0.98; p=0.037). Kaplan-Meier estimates were directionally consistent but not significant (10-year FFDM 66% vs. 52%; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.48-1.02; p=0.060; FFP HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.59-1.05); local, regional and locoregional control (HR 0.80-1.01) and toxicity profiles did not differ. Serum creatinine (p<0.001) and the AE/SAE rate (24.2% vs. 15.4%; p=0.048) were higher with CDDP. ARO 04-01/AHMO did not show superiority of CDDP/5-FU over MMC/5-FU for overall survival. CDDP-based CRT remains the established standard for fit patients; MMC/5-FU is a safe and effective alternative with comparable overall survival and measurably lower nephrotoxicity and cumulative AE/SAE burden for CDDP-contraindicated patients. papers.abstract: Early-onset breast cancer (EOBC), defined in this Review as breast cancer diagnosed before 50 years of age, accounts for a growing proportion of global breast cancer incidence and is associated with disproportionately unfavourable outcomes. Although inherited susceptibility contributes to EOBC risk, the rising incidence and persistent disparities that characterize EOBC cannot be explained by genetics alone; molecular subtype distribution, modifiable exposures and healthcare-related factors also affect presentation, response to treatment and outcomes. In this Review, we synthesize epidemiological trends, providing an overview of the inherited and multifactorial risk determinants, tumour subtype distributions and modifiable exposures that shape EOBC across populations. We examine why age-based screening paradigms do not fully capture EOBC risk and discuss approaches to risk-informed early detection and diagnosis, emphasizing the need for prompt histopathological confirmation and biomarker-guided care. We then address structural and healthcare-related barriers that constrain implementation of such an approach, including diagnostic capacity, pathology infrastructure, treatment affordability and financial toxicity. Finally, we propose a roadmap for the prevention, early diagnosis and interception of EOBC that integrates family history, germline testing, ancestry-aware risk models, pathology, treatment access and resource-stratified implementation. We argue that biological risk architecture must be aligned with healthcare systems that translate risk recognition into prompt, equitable and optimal management, including appropriately adapted treatment, ultimately improving outcomes for patients with EOBC.

papers.abstract: The risk of developing dementia at any given age has fallen steadily in Europe and the United States over recent decades. A key unresolved question is whether recent generations reach older age with better cognitive capacity, experience slower cognitive decline, or both, as this has implications for when preventive interventions are likely to have the greatest impact. Analyzing ~783,000 episodic-memory assessments from ~219,000 individuals in five longitudinal studies followed for up to 30 years, we find that later-born generations benefit from a double dividend, with higher memory levels entering old age and slower decline thereafter. The combined advantage is large enough to plausibly account for the reported 13% per-decade decline in dementia incidence. Improvements are concentrated among the fastest decliners; later-born generations show longer periods of stable memory, and their slower decline is mirrored by lower rates of clinical impairment and slower hippocampal atrophy. Calendar-time trends affecting all generations simultaneously are unlikely to explain these differences. Because memory level is built mainly in early life whereas the rate of decline is shaped by conditions in adulthood, sustaining the decline in dementia incidence will require prevention policies that protect brain health across the whole lifespan, beginning in childhood.

papers.abstract: The hyperinflammatory phenotype of acute respiratory failure (ARF) identifies patients with high mortality, but its underlying pathophysiology remains incompletely understood. Mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to inflammation, oxidative stress, and cell injury in critical illness. We investigated whether plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins characterize the hyperinflammatory phenotype and whether they contribute to its association with mortality. We analyzed 285 emergency department patients with ARF and suspected or confirmed COVID-19. Inflammatory phenotypes were derived by latent class analysis using nine biomarkers and clinical indicators. A mitochondrial-protein score was calculated from 59 MitoCarta3.0-matched proteins, and mitochondrial clusters were derived by principal component analysis and k-means clustering. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Latent class analysis identified 185 hypoinflammatory (65%) and 100 hyperinflammatory (35%) patients, with a significant difference in 28-day mortality (14/185, 7.6% vs. 31/100, 31.0%; p < 0.001). The mitochondrial-protein score increased with the probability of hyperinflammation (ρ=0.46, p < 0.001). Forty-three of 59 mitochondrial-associated proteins were more abundant in the hyperinflammatory phenotype, with prominent differences in apoptosis regulation, oxidative stress, and oxidative phosphorylation proteins. In a mutually adjusted model, the hyperinflammatory phenotype remained associated with mortality (odds ratio [OR]=6.40, 95%CI:3.08-13.95; p < 0.001), whereas the mitochondrial-protein score was not (OR=0.83 per SD, 95%CI:0.58-1.17; p = 0.30). Mitochondrial clusters yielded consistent findings. The hyperinflammatory phenotype of ARF is characterized by increased plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins, linking inflammation with mitochondrial biology and cellular injury. This mitochondrial signature did not account for mortality independently of inflammatory phenotype, suggesting that it represents a biological component of the hyperinflammatory state.

papers.abstract: To determine the overall postoperative outcome and success, it is important to assess the occurrence of postoperative complications as well as patients' perception of their health outcomes. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between self-reported quality of recovery and postoperative complications. This secondary analysis included data from three prospective observational studies evaluating quality of recovery in patients undergoing elective non-cardiac surgery. Self-reported quality of recovery was assessed using the Quality of Recovery-15 questionnaire (QoR-15), which was completed by patients preoperatively and on the first postoperative day. Postoperative complications were recorded between surgery and hospital discharge according to the Clavien-Dindo classification (CDC) of surgical complications. Binary logistic regression models were used to assess the association between self-reported quality of recovery and postoperative complications. A total of 1,151 patients were included in this secondary analysis. Of these, 361 (31.4%) experienced postoperative complications. The median difference between preoperative and postoperative QoR-15 sum scores was higher in patients with postoperative complications compared to patients without complications (34 [IQR: 15-51] vs. 22 [IQR: 7-41]; p < 0.001). We found a relevant association between a greater decline in QoR-15 scores from preoperative to first postoperative day and postoperative complications after adjusting for potential confounders (OR 1.18 [95% CI: 1.14;1.23], p < 0.001). The association with no or minor complications was stronger in heterogeneous populations with various types of surgical procedures than in patients with radical prostatectomy. Early self-reported quality of recovery is associated with the occurrence of postoperative complications after elective non-cardiac surgery. Whether this association may aid in identifying patients at risk of developing postoperative complications warrants further investigation.

papers.abstract: The choice of vasopressor during Caesarean delivery to prevent maternal hypotension remains debated. This study aimed to determine the concentration-dependent effects of vasopressors on pregnant myometrium, with and without oxytocin. In this prospective ex vivo study, myometrial samples were obtained from full-term pregnant women during elective Caesarean delivery. Myometrial contractility to vasopressors was recorded in the absence/presence of oxytocin compared with controls. Concentration-response testing was done with ephedrine, phenylephrine, and norepinephrine. The primary outcome was the motility index (amplitude×frequency). Isolated primary myometrial cells were also used for calcium mobilisation assays. Myometrial samples were obtained from 32 females. The mean motility index increased with ephedrine (+39.9%; 95% CI 20.6-62.5; P<0.001) and phenylephrine (+36.2%; 95% CI 19.3-55.4; P<0.001), but norepinephrine had no effect (+12.0%; 95% CI -0.7 to 26.1; P=0.066) compared with control. Similar changes in motility index were observed in the presence of oxytocin. Calcium mobilisation recordings on primary myometrial cells supported the contractility findings, with increases in intracellular calcium ions after ephedrine and phenylephrine, but not with norepinephrine compared with control. Ephedrine and phenylephrine increased ex vivo human myometrial contractility, both independently and in combination with oxytocin, consistent with improving uterine tone during Caesarean delivery. Norepinephrine does not affect myometrial contractility, suggesting that it is safe to use before delivery.

papers.abstract: Preclinical evidence suggests synergy between poly-ADP-ribose inhibitors and camptothecin chemotherapy. We tested the talazoparib and irinotecan combination (TI) in the neoadjuvant setting in the I-SPY2 trial in patients with HER2-negative locally advanced breast cancer. I-SPY2 is a phase II platform trial for stage 2/3 early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence. Participants were adaptively randomized to one of several experimental neoadjuvant therapies or control based on receptor subtypes defined by hormone receptor (HR), HER2 status, and MammaPrint risk (MP1, MP2). The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (pCR). Treatments 'graduate' if/when they achieve an 85% Bayesian probability of success in a subtype-specific phase III trial. Only HER2-negative patients were eligible for randomization to the TI arm. All patients received weekly paclitaxel for 12 weeks, followed by doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide and surgery. Participants randomized to the TI arm received daily oral talazoparib and irinotecan infusions every other week. Pathway-specific biomarkers were assessed for response prediction. The combination of talazoparib and irinotecan failed to graduate from the I-SPY2 trial, with a 19% modeled posterior probability of pCR in the TI arm compared with 20% in the control arm among all patients with HER2-negative breast cancer. The most common adverse events were neutropenia and anemia in the TI arm and neuropathy and fatigue in the control arm. pCR rates were highest in patients with germline Breast Cancer Gene 1 or 2 (BRCA1/2) mutations receiving TI (pCR rate 50%) and in those with tumors expressing a DNA repair deficiency signature. TI will not be further explored as a combination given lack of improved efficacy over control (paclitaxel) for neoadjuvant treatment in patients with HER2-negative breast cancer. pCR rates were highest (50%) among patients with germline BRCA1/2 mutations, likely due to the efficacy of talazoparib alone. Further combinations could be explored in patients with HER2-negative breast cancer and a germline BRCA1/2 or PALB2 mutation.

papers.abstract: Robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery commonly requires prolonged pneumoperitoneum and steep Trendelenburg positioning, which promote perioperative atelectasis and may increase complication risk. We aimed to investigate the effect of low pneumoperitoneum pressure (LPP) on atelectasis following robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery. We conducted a prospective, surgeon- and assessor-blind, randomised controlled trial in women undergoing elective robot-assisted laparoscopic gynaecological surgery. Participants were randomly allocated to the LPP (12 mmHg) or standard pneumoperitoneum pressure (SPP: 15 mmHg) group. Primary outcomes were modified lung ultrasound (mLUS) scores assessed after surgery and 30 min post-extubation. Secondary outcomes included incidence of atelectasis, percentage of desaturation in the post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU), lengths of PACU and hospital stay, surgeon satisfaction with the operative visual field, numeric rating scale pain score and modified clinical pulmonary infection score on postoperative day 1, and postoperative pulmonary complications 7 days postoperatively. Sixty patients were enrolled (30 per group). The mLUSs were significantly lower in the LPP group versus the SPP group postoperatively (P < 0.001) and 30 min post-extubation (P < 0.001), particularly in the posterolateral lung region (P < 0.001). Compared with the SPP group, the LPP group experienced a 1.59-fold reduction in the risk of postoperative atelectasis 30 min post-extubation in the PACU (P = 0.004). Other secondary outcomes showed no significant intergroup differences. A low pneumoperitoneum pressure during robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery reduced perioperative modified lung ultrasound scores and the incidence of early postoperative atelectasis. However, this imaging difference was not accompanied by significant improvements in oxygenation. Further studies powered for clinical pulmonary outcomes are needed. papers.abstract: This study evaluated efficacy and safety of intraoperative individualized stepwise positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) titration guided by lung ultrasound (LUS) in reducing pulmonary atelectasis and complications in patients undergoing robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy or cystectomy (RARPC). This randomized trial included 88 patients undergoing elective RARPC. Patients were assigned to either standard ventilation (PEEP 4 cmH₂O; group C) or LUS-guided stepwise PEEP titration up to 12 cmH₂O (group R). Patients, outcome assessors, and the data analyst were blinded. The primary outcome was analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model, estimating the between-group difference in LUS score at 2 h after surgery. Group R showed significantly lower total LUS scores at 2 h after surgery (adjusted difference: -1.68, 95%CI: -2.89 to -0.47; p = 0.007) compared to group C. Likewise, significantly lower LUS scores were observed in Group R from the end of surgery onward. PEEP titration progressively reduced post-pneumoperitoneum atelectasis rates from 50% to 9.1%, at a highest PEEP level of 12 cmH₂O. Dynamic lung compliance in group R was significantly greater at Top compared with the control group (58.93 ± 3.48 vs. 49.91 ± 5.74 mL/cmH₂O; p < 0.001). Heart rate, mean arterial pressure, oxygen saturation, and end-tidal CO₂ were comparable at all time points. Both groups were comparable for intraoperative hypotension and bradycardia. Intraoperative LUS-guided individualized PEEP optimization significantly reduced the incidence of postoperative atelectasis and improved dynamic lung compliance without compromising hemodynamic stability in patients undergoing RARPC. Lung ultrasound offers a practical, effective, and non-invasive bedside tool for optimizing ventilation in high-risk surgical settings. This study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov in March 2024 (ID: NCT06307704). The trial protocol is available through the ClinicalTrials.gov registry at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06307704 .

papers.abstract: Quarterly echocardiographic surveillance during trastuzumab-based human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-directed therapy was established in the early 2000s. With lower left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) decline rates with newer regimens, the justification for frequent cardiac surveillance warrants re-evaluation. We carried out a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis of clinical trials of patients receiving trastuzumab, trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1), or trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), using pooled estimates of study-reported cardiac dysfunction, predominantly decreased LVEF, to evaluate echocardiographic surveillance strategies. For early-stage disease (12-month treatment duration), strategies evaluated included baseline echocardiography plus imaging at 6 months, baseline plus imaging at 6 and 12 months, and baseline plus imaging at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. For metastatic disease (continuous treatment), strategies included baseline echocardiography plus annual imaging, baseline plus imaging every 6 months, and baseline plus imaging every 3 months. Fifty-seven studies conducted from 1999 to 2026 (37 847 patients) were included. Pooled rates of study-reported cardiac dysfunction, predominantly decreased LVEF, were 4.5%, 1.7%, and 1.4% for trastuzumab, T-DXd, and T-DM1, respectively, in early-stage disease, and 7.7%, 3.3%, and 2.3%, respectively, in metastatic disease; grade 3 events were rare. At a willingness-to-pay threshold of $120 000/quality-adjusted life year (QALY), baseline echocardiography plus one follow-up study at 6 months was preferred for early-stage trastuzumab, whereas baseline-only imaging was preferred for early-stage T-DM1 and T-DXd. Monitoring every 3 months was not cost-effective for any early-stage regimen, with incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) of $12 974 923/QALY for trastuzumab, $3 033 636/QALY for T-DM1, and $4 388 134/QALY for T-DXd. In metastatic disease, baseline-only imaging was preferred for all three regimens; annual monitoring exceeded the willingness-to-pay threshold for trastuzumab, T-DM1, and T-DXd, with ICERs of $191 781/QALY, $537 175/QALY, and $353 098/QALY, respectively. Echocardiography every 3 months was not cost-effective for any regimen or disease setting. Monitoring should be regimen- and setting-specific, with prospective validation of less intensive strategies. These findings are only applicable to lower-risk, trial-eligible patients.

papers.abstract: Therapeutic cancer vaccines reliably induce tumour-specific immune responses, although translating this immunogenicity into durable tumour control remains a major challenge. This disconnect is probably the result of a series of biological bottlenecks, from antigen selection and presentation to T cell priming, tumour infiltration and resistance to immune suppression. Advances in neoantigen identification, vaccine technologies, immune profiling and computational biology have renewed and re-energized the field. Emerging evidence from clinical trials testing neoantigen-directed vaccines indicates that therapeutic vaccination can improve clinical outcomes particularly when applied in earlier disease settings and integrated within broader immunotherapeutic strategies. In this Review, we examine the mechanisms limiting vaccine efficacy, discuss how they are informing the design of next-generation vaccines, and explore the biomarkers and therapeutic strategies that might enable vaccination to achieve more consistent clinical benefit.

papers.abstract: Perioperative ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) remains a significant cause of postoperative organ dysfunction and mortality after cardiac, vascular, transplant, and high-risk noncardiac surgery. Despite advances in anesthetic and surgical techniques, practical strategies to prevent IRI are limited. Growing evidence indicates that purinergic signaling, mediated by extracellular ATP, ADP, adenosine, and their receptors, centrally regulates inflammation, microvascular function, and tissue recovery during perioperative ischemia and reperfusion. This narrative review synthesizes preclinical, translational, and clinical evidence on purinergic mechanisms in perioperative IRI across major organ systems, including the heart, lungs, kidneys, liver, intestines, and brain, emphasizing pharmacological strategies and anesthetic interactions relevant to intraoperative and early postoperative management. During ischemia and early reperfusion, extracellular ATP released from injured cells activates P2 receptors, promoting inflammasome activation, endothelial dysfunction, and microcirculatory injury. Subsequent hydrolysis of ATP by ectonucleotidases CD39 and CD73 generates adenosine, which activates P1 receptors (Adora1, Adora2a, Adora2b, and Adora3) to suppress inflammation, improve perfusion, and enhance tissue protection. Hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-dependent upregulation of CD73 and A2B transcriptionally amplifies this ATP-to-adenosine transition, and miRNAs post-transcriptionally modulate it. Pharmacological approaches targeting these pathways represent promising strategies for perioperative organ protection, whereas clinical evidence supporting anesthetic regimen selection for purinergic modulation remains insufficient. The efficacy of conditioning strategies, including ischemic preconditioning and remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC), remains controversial, with negative large-scale trials highlighting the translational gap between preclinical models and multimorbid surgical patients. Purinergic signaling provides a unifying mechanistic framework for perioperative ischemia-reperfusion injury and represents a promising target for pharmacological organ protection. Prioritize pharmacological strategies that enhance adenosine generation, activate protective adenosine receptors, or inhibit ATP-P2X7-driven inflammation in perioperative clinical trials. Understanding how comorbidities and concomitant medications modulate purinergic pathways is essential for successful clinical translation.

papers.abstract: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab improves survival in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. We evaluated this combination as neoadjuvant therapy and investigated its effect on peripheral immunity and the tumour microenvironment. PRIME-HCC is a single-arm, phase 1b trial in adults (aged ≥18 years) with early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, Child-Pugh A liver function, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1. Patients received nivolumab (3 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 22 of the first and second cycle) and ipilimumab (1 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 of the first cycle only) before liver resection. The primary endpoint was safety, assessed by treatment-related delays to surgery and adverse events in the intention-to-treat population. Translational analyses included imaging mass cytometry and spatial transcriptomics on paired tumour samples, peripheral immunophenotyping, T-cell receptor (TCR) β sequencing, and longitudinal tumour-agnostic circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) profiling. This trial was registered with EudraCT (2018-000987-27) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03682276); follow-up is currently ongoing. Between Sept 18, 2019, and Sept 28, 2023, of 43 patients assessed for eligibility, 33 patients were enrolled (25 [76%] male and 8 [24%] female; median age 68 years [range 38-80; IQR 63-73]); median follow-up was 25·7 months (95% CI 21·2-30·1). Any-grade adverse events occurred in 31 (94%) of patients, with treatment-related adverse events (trAEs) in 25 (76%) patients. Grade 3 trAEs occurred in three (9%) patients (transaminase elevation, anaemia, and dyspnoea). Serious adverse events were recorded in three (9%) patients, and no grade 4-5 events or treatment-related deaths occurred. 30 (91%) patients underwent surgery, including two (6%) who had immune checkpoint inhibitor-related surgical delays. Objective response rate by RECIST 1.1 was noted in eight (25%; 95% CI 13-42) patients (one complete response and seven partial responses), with 31 (97%; 84-100) patients achieving disease control. The absence of ctDNA after surgery was associated with improved 2-year recurrence-free survival (nine [82%] of 11 patients vs two [29%] of seven; p=0·049), as was at least 50% ctDNA reduction (median not reached [95% CI not reached] vs 20·9 months [95% CI 16·3-25·4]; HR 0·14 [95% CI 0·02-0·91]; p=0·039). Patients with objective responses showed expansion of peripheral PD-1-positive, Ki-67-positive, CD8-positive T cells (T-responding exhausted cells [Tresp]), associated with higher baseline intratumoral progenitor-exhausted T cells (Tpex) and increased Tresp infiltration. Patients whose disease did not respond to treatment exhibited enrichment of terminally exhausted CD8-positive T cells (Tex-term; CD8-positive PD-1-positive TOX-positive cells) and regulatory T cells. Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab is feasible in early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, and later-phase randomised trials are needed to confirm the efficacy of this treatment strategy. Longitudinal ctDNA monitoring could support detection of minimal residual disease and warrants further prospective validation. papers.abstract: Patient experience is a core dimension of oncology care quality, but cognitive burden, emotional distress, and complex care trajectories in brain metastases populations may limit traditional survey approaches. This study evaluated the feasibility and interpretability of a locally developed, self-administered patient experience survey administered after initial brain-directed intervention within a multidisciplinary brain metastases program. We conducted a prospective quality improvement evaluation of a patient experience survey administered on tablets at follow-up visits two to three months after initial consultation. Eligible participants were new patients seen in a multidisciplinary brain metastases clinic. Descriptive statistics characterized response patterns, including agreement rates, "not applicable" responses, and missing data. Reasons for non-completion were categorized descriptively. Among 70 eligible patients, 41 completed the survey (59%). Overall ratings were high, with most respondents reporting that they were always treated with courtesy and respect and always received the best care possible. Communication and decision-making items showed high agreement. Treatment-dependent items showed reduced applicability, including explanations of medication and treatment impact on daily activities, with substantial "not applicable" responses. A subset strongly disagreed with items addressing clarity of results and functional impact. Open-ended responses were generally positive despite structured disagreement. Surveys administered after brain-directed intervention yielded high overall experience ratings but revealed variation in domain applicability, which may reflect treatment exposure and position along the disease trajectory. As a single cross-sectional administration of an instrument without formal psychometric validation, these findings primarily inform survey feasibility and design; trajectory-informed assessment strategies warrant prospective evaluation.

papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of B-cell malignancies, but insufficient expansion and persistence, progressive T-cell dysfunction, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments continue to limit durable efficacy and broader application. Cytokines are central regulators of both T-cell fitness and interactions with surrounding immune cells, providing a rationale for incorporating cytokine signals directly into engineered cellular therapies. Here we trace the development and clinical translation of cytokine-enhanced CAR T cells from the pioneering studies with IL-12 to common g-chain cytokines and IL-18. IL-12 established the potential of engineered T cells to deliver potent inflammatory signals locally and mobilize endogenous immunity, but also revealed the risk of systemic inflammatory toxicity. Common g-chain cytokines, particularly IL-7, IL-15 and IL-21, have predominantly been exploited to promote expansion, persistence and favorable differentiation states, with several approaches advancing to clinical testing. IL-18 combines direct support of engineered T cells with recruitment and remodeling of endogenous immune compartments and has recently demonstrated encouraging clinical activity in hematologic malignancies. Emerging strategies increasingly extend beyond cytokine secretion to inducible circuits, synthetic cytokine receptors, unconventional cytokines and combinations of complementary signals. Rational selection of cytokines for specific disease contexts, together with precise spatial and temporal control of their activity, will be critical to balance efficacy against toxicity and realize the full potential of cytokine-engineered cellular therapies.

papers.abstract: To compare image quality and radiation-dose indices between photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) and conventional energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) examinations in patients with multiple myeloma. This retrospective intraindividual study included 47 patients with non-contrast whole-body PCCT examinations (NAEOTOM Alpha, Siemens Healthineers) and prior EID-CT examinations (SOMATOM Sensation 64, Siemens Healthineers). Examinations were performed using the respective clinical protocols, which differed in acquisition and reconstruction settings. Quantitative image analysis included region-of-interest measurements in the lungs, spleen, muscle, and adipose tissue. Image noise and signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) were calculated. For qualitative assessment, two radiologists independently evaluated randomized and anonymized PCCT and EID-CT scans of the same patients using a 5-point Likert scale to rate overall image quality, sharpness, noise, and osteolytic lesion conspicuity. Qualitative ratings were compared separately for each reader using two-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Differences in CT-dose-index, dose-length-product, and quantitative image metrics were analyzed using two-sided paired t-tests. Quantitative analysis demonstrated significantly lower image noise in PCCT compared to EID-CT in the spleen, muscle, and adipose tissue (p < 0.0001), but not in lung tissue (p = 0.27). SNR was significantly higher with PCCT in all tissues except the lungs (p < 0.0001; lungs: p = 0.22; adipose tissue: p = 0.02). Qualitative assessment showed that PCCT was rated significantly better than EID-CT for overall image quality, image sharpness, noise, and osteolysis conspicuity (p < 0.0001 for all categories). Radiation dose parameters (CTDIvol and DLP) were significantly lower with PCCT than with EID-CT (p < 0.0001). In non-contrast whole-body imaging of patients with multiple myeloma, the evaluated PCCT system provided superior image quality and significantly lower radiation-dose indices than the historical EID-CT system. These findings reflect the combined performance of the imaging systems and their respective acquisition and reconstruction settings.
